He did not appear in any game.{{citation |url=https://und.com/elam-happy-making-plays-on-defense/|title=Elam Happy Making Plays On Defense|publisher=University of Notre Dame |date=October 11, 2001|accessdate=February 19, 2020}} As a sophomore, he appeared in 11 games, making 29 tackles, 2 interceptions, 2 sacks, one fumble recovery and one forced fumble. As a sophomore in 2002, a felony sexual battery conviction got him expelled from the school.{{citation |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/football/jets/abram-elam-aiming-fresh-start-article-1.256970|title=Abram Elam aiming for fresh start|publisher=New York Daily News |date=November 25, 2007|accessdate=February 19, 2020}} He attended [[Palm Beach Community College]] and worked at a dentist's office. He enrolled at [[Kent State University]] in 2004, but because he initially did not receive a scholarship, the Riviera Beach residents raised US$20,000 to pay for his tuition. As a senior, he appeared in 11 games, making 64 tackles (third on the team), 3 interceptions (tied for the team lead), 4 passes defensed and 6 punts returned for a 9.2-yard average.{{citation |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/news/fl-xpm-2005-06-12-0506110489-story.html|title=FIRST AND FOREMOST, A SECOND CHANCE|publisher=Sun Sentinel |date=June 12, 2005|accessdate=February 19, 2020}} ==Professional career== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 0 | weight = 206 | note = Values from [[Pro Day]]{{Cite web |url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=53771&DraftYear=2005 |title=2005 Draft Scout Abram Elam, Kent State NFL Draft Scout College Football Profile |website=draftscout.com |access-date=April 29, 2022}}{{Cite web |url=https://insider.espn.com/nfl/draft/player/_/id/8344 |title=Abram Elam 2005 NFL Draft Profile |website=insider.espn.com |access-date=April 29, 2022}} }} ===Miami Dolphins=== Elam was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Miami Dolphins]] after the [[2005 NFL draft]] on May 16. He was waived on July 28. ===Dallas Cowboys (first stint)=== On February 2, [[2006 NFL season|2006]], head coach [[Bill Parcells]] signed him as a [[free agent]], based on a recommendation from [[Tucker Frederickson]] who had a son that played at [[Kent State University]]. He registered 15 [[special teams]] tackles (fourth on the team) and 4 kickoff returns for 95 yards. On September 2, [[2007 NFL season|2007]], the team decided to keep [[Courtney Brown (defensive back)|Courtney Brown]] instead of Elam during last cuts of the preseason.{{cite web| url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4680140/abram-elam-should-be-cowboys-safety-choice | title=Abram Elam should be safety choice | accessdate=February 19, 2020}} ===New York Jets=== On September 12, 2007, the [[New York Jets]] signed him based on a recommendation from [[Bill Parcells]] and would start 8 games at [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]]. In [[2008 NFL season|2008]] he started 9 games. In [[2010 NFL season|2010]], he posted 79 tackles, 2 interceptions, 10 passes defensed, 2 forced fumbles and 2 fumble recoveries. ===Dallas Cowboys (second stint)=== On August 3, [[2011 NFL season|2011]], after hiring his former Browns [[defensive coordinator]] [[Rob Ryan]], the Cowboys signed him to a one-year contract as a [[free agent]] and named him the starter at [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]]. {{cite web|author=Todd Archer|author2=Calvin Watkins|title=Abram Elam reunites with Rob Ryan|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nfl/story/_/id/6832246/dallas-cowboys-sign-safety-abram-elam-one-year-deal | publisher=ESPN | date=August 4, 2011 | accessdate=February 19, 2020}} He started every game, while registering 79 tackles (second on the team), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. '''Adam Blayne Schreiber''' ({{respell|sh|RI|ber}}; born February 20, 1962) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] and [[long snapper]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 16 seasons with seven different teams. He played [[college football ]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SchrAd20.htm|title=Adam Schreiber stats|publisher=pro football reference.com|accessdate=1 September 2013}}</ref>

==Early life==
Schreiber attended [[S. R. Butler High School]] where he was a star on the varsity football team, graduating in 1980.<ref name="ahsfhs">{{cite web |publisher=Alabama High School Football Historical Society |title=Butler Rebels |url=http://www.ahsfhs.org/teams2/allstate.asp?Team=Butler |accessdate=August 15, 2013}}</ref>

He then played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]].

==Professional career==
Coming out of college in 1984, he was first drafted by the [[Houston Gamblers]] as a territorial pick in the [[USFL draft]] and then, later in the year, by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the ninth round of the [[1984 NFL draft]]. He signed with the Seahawks and was cut by them at the end of training camp that year, but then re-signed with them five weeks later. He played in six games for the Seahawks as a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]], but was again cut at the start of training camp in 1985.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web |title=Adam Schreiber transactions |url=https://www.prosportstransactions.com/football/Search/SearchResults.php?Player=Adam+Schreiber&Team=&BeginDate=&EndDate=&PlayerMovementChkBx=yes&submit=Search |access-date=5 May 2023}}</ref>

He was signed by the [[New Orleans Saints]] two months later and played one game for them before again being released at the end of training camp. A few weeks later he was signed as a free agent by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] to replace [[Jim Gilmore]].<ref name="transactions"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Football Almanac |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1986/10/17/Football-Almanac/3832529905600/ |access-date=5 May 2023 |date=17 October 1986}}</ref>

In 1987, for the first time in his career, he was the starter all season—missing only the strike games. In the offseason he was signed again by the Eagles and then moved to long snapper. Six games in, he was waived by the Eagles, but then immediately picked up by the [[New York Jets]] finishing the season as their long snapper.<ref name="transactions"/>

In 1989, the Jets moved Schreiber to [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|offensive tackle]]. At the end of that season he became an unrestricted free agent and was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref name="transactions"/>

He signed two more times with the Vikings, after the 1991 and 1992 seasons. He played mostly at center, but all five offensive line positions and handled the long-snapping duties.<ref>{{cite news |title=Vikings sign Newsome and Schreiber |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1990/03/22/Vikings-sign-Newsome-and-Schreiber/4605638082000/ |access-date=5 May 2023 |date=22 March 1990}}</ref> After starting just one game in his first three seasons, he started all 16 in 1993 at center. It the most productive season of his career. Despite his success in 1993, he was cut by the Vikings during the following summer, but picked up by the [[New York Giants]] about a month later.<ref name="transactions"/>

Schreiber played three seasons with Giants, starting four games at center and serving as their long snapper. He was resigned after the 1994 season, but became a free agent after the 1997 one. He was signed in August by the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref name="transactions"/>

Schreiber played three seasons with Falcons as long snapper and center, which included a trip to [[Super Bowl XXXIII]]. He was resigned by them after the Super Bowl, but then released three games into the season, ending his career.<ref name="transactions"/>

==Personal life==
Schreiber is Jewish.<ref name="gb1">{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Xcfef_d2es4C&pg=PA158 |title=The Big Book of Jewish Sports Heroes: An Illustrated Compendium of Sports ... - Peter S. Horvitz|date= April 2007|isbn=9781561719075|accessdate=2013-08-15|last1=Horvitz|first1=Peter S.|publisher=SP Books }}</ref> and currently resides in [[Panama City Beach, Florida]].

'''Adam James Lingner''' (born November 2, 1960) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive lineman]] for 13 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] and the [[Buffalo Bills]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois Fighting Illini]]. Lingner was selected by the Chiefs in the ninth round of the [[1983 NFL draft]], and was the lowest draft pick to make their squad. He was a member of Buffalo's teams in four consecutive [[Super Bowl]] games: [[Super Bowl XXV]], [[Super Bowl XXVI]], [[Super Bowl XXVII]] and [[Super Bowl XXVIII]].

Adam Lingner is most known for being the long-snapper on the "wide right" field goal by [[Scott Norwood]] in [[Super Bowl XXV]].  Lingner is also one of only 22 players to play in all of the Buffalo Bills Super Bowl appearances in the early 1990s.

'''Adam Eugene Carriker''' (born May 6, 1984) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[St. Louis Rams]] in the first round of the [[2007 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]]. He also played for the [[Washington Redskins]].

==Early life==
Carriker was born in [[Hastings, Nebraska]].  He moved to [[Kennewick, Washington]], at the age of three,<ref name=huskersbio>[http://www.huskers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=4&SPID=22&DB_OEM_ID=100&ATCLID=966&Q_SEASON=2006 "Adam Carriker".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181221230556/http://www.huskers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=4&SPID=22&DB_OEM_ID=100&ATCLID=966&Q_SEASON=2006 |date=2018-12-21 }}  [http://www.huskers.com/ Huskers.com.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200123021912/https://huskers.com/ |date=2020-01-23 }}  Retrieved 2016-02-14.</ref> and attended [[Kennewick High School]], where he played quarterback and defensive end. He was a three-year starter at quarterback and team captain for three years. In his only season at defensive end (his senior season), he recorded 25 tackles, 15 sacks, and four forced fumbles in a winless season. Regardless, he was named to Second-team All-Big 9 Honors. Carriker visited Oregon, Oregon State and Washington State before committing to Nebraska. Additionally, Carriker was a three-time All-Conference selection in baseball.

==College career==
Carriker [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]]ed in 2002. In his 2003 freshman season he played extensively in passing situations before injuring his ankle against Utah State. Against the [[Colorado Buffaloes football|University of Colorado]] he had three quarterback hurries and ended a CU drive in the third quarter with a nine-yard sack of quarterback [[Joel Klatt]]. He finished the year with three tackles and three quarterback hurries. He played in his first bowl game, the 2003 Alamo Bowl after the regular season. In his 2004 sophomore year Carriker was hampered for the second straight season by an ankle injury. He played in 10 games with eight starts in the 2004 campaign, and finished with 36 tackles, including seven tackles for loss and three sacks for 18 yards. Carriker added seven quarterback hurries during his sophomore season.

As a junior in 2005 Carriker started all 12 games at the base end spot, and finished with 9.5 sacks for 84 yards and 17 tackles for loss for 96 yards. His 9½ sacks tied for the Big 12 Conference lead and ranked 19th nationally. He also led Nebraska with 21 quarterback hurries, 10 more than any other Husker defender. Carriker's 43 total tackles ranked seventh on the team and tied for the most among defensive linemen. He began his junior season by notching two of the Huskers' school-record tying 11 sacks in the team's 25–7 win over Maine. Carriker capped 2005 with one tackle in the [[Alamo Bowl]] victory over the [[University of Michigan]]. Adam was voted 2005 Nebraska Defensive MVP.

As a senior in 2006 Adam Carriker completed a dominant career in the 2006 season [[Cotton Bowl Classic]] against [[Auburn University]]. In 2006, Carriker earned Nebraska's Defensive MVP honor for the second straight season, and was honored as the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year by the league's coaches. Carriker finished the season with a team-leading seven sacks and ranked second on the team with 16 tackles behind the line of scrimmage. His 52 total tackles led all Nebraska defensive linemen, and he also paced the Blackshirt defense with 12 quarterback hurries, while registering his first career interception. In addition to his selection as Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year, Carriker was a First-team All-Big 12 pick by the [[Big 12]] Coaches and the [[Associated Press]]. He was also a Third-team All-America selection by [[Rivals.com]].

The strong senior season put Carriker's name in a prominent position in the NU record books. He finished with 41 career tackles for loss to rank fifth in the program's history. Carriker has 20½ career sacks to rank sixth on the Cornhusker charts. Carriker graduated with a degree in business administration.

===St. Louis Rams===
Carriker was selected in the first round, with the 13th overall pick, by the St. Louis Rams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On July 26, 2007, Carriker signed a five-year $14.5 million contract, with guarantees of $9.5 million.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-07-27 |title=NFC: Rams sign first-round pick Carriker |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/trainingcamp07/news/story?id=2951187 |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> Carriker started all 16 games of his rookie season at defensive tackle instead of his college position, defensive end.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 St. Louis Rams Roster & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/ram/2007_roster.htm |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Carriker, who bulked up from the 296 pounds he weighed at the [[NFL Scouting Combine]], weighed in the 305-pound range during the 2007 season.

He was voted the Rams Rookie of the Year called the [[Carroll Rosenbloom]] Memorial Award, finishing with 2 sacks, 32 tackles, and a safety.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Carriker 2007 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CarrAd99/gamelog/2007/ |access-date=2025-04-12 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Carriker missed the entire 2009 NFL season due to injury.<ref name="v518">{{cite web | title=Carriker's season over after Rams place him on injured reserve | website=NFL.com | date=2009-09-05 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/carriker-s-season-over-after-rams-place-him-on-injured-reserve-09000d5d812677d4 | access-date=2024-12-18}}</ref>

=== Washington Redskins ===
Carriker was traded to the [[Washington Redskins]] on April 20, 2010. In exchange, the teams swapped fifth and seventh-round draft picks in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Michael David |title=Rams trade Adam Carriker to Redskins |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2010/04/20/rams-trade-adam-carriker-to-redskins/ |publisher=[[Profootballtalk.com]] |date=April 20, 2010 |access-date=2010-04-21| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100422005314/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2010/04/20/rams-trade-adam-carriker-to-redskins/| archive-date= 22 April 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> After initial shock, Carriker was pleased about his trade and the chance to revitalize his career.<ref>{{cite web |author=Carriker, Adam |title=Hog Blog with Adam Carriker |url=http://www.the-hogs.net/blogs/2010/09/09/hog-blog-with-adam-carriker-week-1/ |publisher=The-Hogs.net|date=September 12, 2010 |access-date=2010-09-21}}</ref>

In Washington, Carriker earned the starting left defensive end position for the Washington Redskins in a 3-4 defensive scheme. With the Rams he was a "3-technique" defensive tackle in a 4-3 defensive scheme which did not work out and led to his trade to the Washington Redskins. "In St. Louis, we tried to make him a 3-technique and up-the-field rusher," said defensive coordinator [[Jim Haslett]]. "For a guy who ran the 40 in 4.7 and was 6-6, 315 pounds, you'd think he could do that. But that's not what he wants to do. He wants to play with strength and power, and he does a pretty good job of it. He feels so much more comfortable in this."<ref>{{cite web |author=Campbell, Rich |title=Carriker, Barron old foes |url=http://fredericksburg.com/News/FLS/2010/092010/09102010/574438 |publisher=Fredericksburgh.com |date=September 12, 2010 |access-date=2010-09-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120404031822/http://fredericksburg.com/News/FLS/2010/092010/09102010/574438 |archive-date=April 4, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Carriker's 315 pounds is ideal, and he reported at the beginning of the 2010 season that he bench pressed 500 pounds, which helps him in his new position.<ref>{{cite web |author=Carriker, Adam |title=Hog Blog with Adam Carriker |url=http://www.the-hogs.net/blogs/2010/09/09/hog-blog-with-adam-carriker-week-1/ |publisher=The-Hogs.net|date=September 12, 2010 |access-date=2010-09-21}}</ref>

Early in the 2010 season the change drew positive reviews, said Rich Campbell of Fredericksburg.com, "I'm buying Carriker as an impact 3-4 end right now. He's strong enough to set the edge on running plays, and he's even generating a pass rush on occasion.  Carriker stopped Houston RB [[Arian Foster]] for a 2-yard loss in the second quarter after he made a quick step inside the pulling left guard. He also beat a double team on the first play of the second half to stop Foster for a gain of one. Carriker isn't dominant—but he is flashing."<ref>{{cite web |author=Campbell, Rich |title=Game Balls, Gassers and Observations: Texans 30, Redskins 27 |url=http://blogs.fredericksburg.com/redskinsjournal/2010/09/21/game-balls-gassers-and-observations-texans-30-redskins-27/ |publisher=Fredericksburgh.com |date=September 12, 2010 |access-date=2010-09-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100924033044/http://blogs.fredericksburg.com/redskinsjournal/2010/09/21/game-balls-gassers-and-observations-texans-30-redskins-27/ |archive-date=24 September 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On March 13, 2012, Carriker re-signed with the Washington Redskins for four years on a $20 million contract with $7 million guaranteed.<ref>{{cite news |agency=AP |url=https://ca.news.yahoo.com/despite-cap-penalty-redskins-aggressive-free-agency-add-230126945.html |title=Despite cap penalty, Redskins go aggressive in free agency, add WRs Garcon and Morgan |access-date=May 18, 2018 |url-status=dead |last=White |first=Joseph |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519030031/https://ca.news.yahoo.com/despite-cap-penalty-redskins-aggressive-free-agency-add-230126945.html |archive-date=2018-05-19 }}</ref> In Week 2 of the [[2012 NFL season|2012 season]] against the [[St. Louis Rams]], he suffered a right knee injury early in the first quarter. The next day it was confirmed that he tore quad tendon in his right leg and he would need surgery and would be placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite news|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2012/09/17/brian-orakpo-adam-carriker-done-for-season/|last=Jones|first=Mike|title=Brian Orakpo, Adam Carriker done for season|date=September 17, 2012|access-date=2012-09-17}}</ref>

Carriker had his contract restructured to help with the salary cap penalty that the Washington Redskins faced last season on March 11, 2013.<ref>{{cite news|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2013/03/11/adam-carriker-restructures-contract-with-redskins/|title=Adam Carriker restructures contract with Redskins|first=Mike|last=Jones|date=March 11, 2013|access-date=2013-03-11}}</ref> On July 25, he was placed on the PUP list after the team announced that he had a third surgery on his right knee and would be out for four or five months.<ref>{{cite news|work=FoxNews.com|url=http://www.foxnews.com/sports/2013/07/25/redskins-de-adam-carriker-out-4-5-months-after-3rd-knee-surgery-placed-on-pup/|title=Redskins' DE Adam Carriker out 4-5 months after 3rd knee surgery, placed on PUP list|date=July 25, 2013|access-date=2013-07-25}}</ref> On December 12, he was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite news|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2013/12/12/carrikers-quest-to-return-officially-comes-to-an-end/|title=Carriker's quest to return officially comes to an end|first=Mike|last=Jones|date=December 12, 2013|access-date=2013-12-19}}</ref> He was released on March 4, 2014.<ref>{{cite news|last=Jones|first=Mike|title=Redskins part ways with Adam Carriker, Sav Rocca, three others|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2014/03/04/redskins-part-ways-with-adam-carriker-sav-rocca-three-others/|newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=4 March 2014}}</ref>

Carriker participated in the first [[NFL Scouting Combine#Veteran combine|NFL Veteran Combine]] in March 2015.<ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-to-host-inaugural-veteran-combine-0ap3000000478211|title=NFL to host inaugural Veteran Combine|date=March 11, 2015|access-date=2015-03-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/adam-carriker-i-m-still-alive-i-can-still-play-this-game-0ap3000000480570|title=Adam Carriker: 'I'm still alive. I can still play this game'|first=Conor|last=Orr|date=March 22, 2015|access-date=2015-03-22}}</ref> He was the only player at the Veteran Combine to do the bench press and performed 40 reps of 225 pounds, which was three more reps than the highest total at the 2015 NFL Combine.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-1/4-Standouts-from-2015s-Veteran-Combine/3cbbf02f-9185-4fe2-aad6-223e615b2b54 | title=4 Standouts from 2015's Veteran Combine | publisher=buccaneers.com | date=March 23, 2015 | access-date=March 6, 2018 | author=Kania, Joe | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180307021446/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-1/4-Standouts-from-2015s-Veteran-Combine/3cbbf02f-9185-4fe2-aad6-223e615b2b54 | archive-date=March 7, 2018 | url-status=dead }}</ref> In April 2015, he attended minicamp with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] on tryout basis.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2015/04/28/quinn-leads-first-mini-camp-practice-as-falcons-coach/26536173/ | title=Quinn leads first mini-camp practice as Falcons coach | publisher=usatoday.com | agency=[[Associated Press]] | date=April 28, 2015 | access-date=March 6, 2018}}</ref>

==Post-playing career==
Carriker has used his Business degree and his TV prowess to appear multiple times on Fox News and Fox Business, as a frequently requested business and political analyst.

Carriker has also made multiple public appearances with Nebraska congressional representatives in Washington, D.C.

Carriker also does weekly national writing and radio segments called the "Carriker Chronicles," where he discusses the current state of the NFL and Nebraska Cornhusker football. His other weekly show appearances include "Chad Dukes vs The World" on the largest sports station in Washington, D.C., to discuss his opinion and give his take on the Washington Commanders game every week. In the state of Nebraska he appears every week on "The Bottom Line," the largest sports talk show in the state which is hosted by Mike'l Severe, to give his take on the state of Nebraska football as well.

In April 2012, Carriker began his radio career as co-host of ''4th & Pain'' along with Chuck Carroll. Carriker, an avid [[WWE]] fan, touts ''4th & Pain'' as being the only pro wrestling and football radio show hosted by an NFL player and a guy who lost 250 pounds, an homage to his co-host.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://4thandpain.com/about-4th-pain/ | title=4th & Pain: About The Show |date=April 2012 |publisher=4thAndPain.com}}</ref> The show airs weekly online.

The show has gained in popularity and they've interviewed NFL stars such as [[Robert Griffin III]], [[DeAngelo Hall]] and [[Chris Cooley]]. In June 2012, the show gained notoriety among wrestling fans after Carriker conducted his first interview with WWE wrestler [[Heath Slater]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://4thandpain.com/2012/06/4th-pain-wwe-superstar-heath-slater-interview-aj-is-crazy-vince-and-vader-are-back-wwe-no-way-out-picks-and-redskins-news/ | title=4th & Pain: WWE Superstar Heath Slater Interview, Vince McMahon Is Back And Redskins News |date=June 16, 2012 |publisher=4thAndPain.com}}</ref> Since then the show and its audience has continued to grow with interviews of wrestling stars such as [[Jeff Hardy]], [[Roman Reigns]] and [[Bill Goldberg]]. Goldberg has appeared on the show himself over 20 different times. He has a cited a friendship with Carriker during his interviews on the show as the reason for his frequent appearances. The show also talks Nebraska football from time to time and has had such Husker legends as [[Eric Crouch]] and [[Tommie Frazier]] join them.

Carriker has also served as a recurring motivational speaker as well.

'''Adam Podlesh''' (born August 11, 1983) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Punter (gridiron football)|punter]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland Terrapins]], and is the only player in school history to be on the All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] team for four years. His punting average of 43.1 yards ranks second in school history. He also played for the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] and [[Chicago Bears]] of the NFL.

==Early life==
Podlesh, who is Jewish,<ref name="JSR911">{{Cite journal |date=September–October 2011 |title=2011 NFL Football Preview |journal=Jewish Sports Review |volume=8 |issue=87 |pages=6–7}}</ref> is a graduate of [[Pittsford Sutherland High School]] in [[Pittsford, New York]]<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 24, 2009 |title=Pigskin Hebrews, 2009 edition |url=http://www.jweekly.com/article/full/40004/pigskin-hebrews-2009-edition-new-flicks-more-new-tv-jews/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100206193437/http://jweekly.com/article/full/40004/pigskin-hebrews-2009-edition-new-flicks-more-new-tv-jews/ |archive-date=February 6, 2010 |access-date=May 31, 2010 |newspaper=J |publisher=Jweekly.com}}</ref> and is a three-time [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] in [[high school football|football]]. Podlesh also played defense and offense for Pittsford Sutherland. On defense, he recorded 92 tackles and five sacks. On offense, he recorded 638 rushing yards and nine touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Podlesh Bio |url=http://www.umterps.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=29700&ATCLID=208127600 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171116030403/http://www.umterps.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=29700&ATCLID=208127600 |archive-date=November 16, 2017 |access-date=November 15, 2017 |website=University of Maryland Athletics |language=en}}</ref>

Podlesh was also a standout athlete for the [[Pittsford Sutherland High School]] track team. He posted the fastest [[200 metres]] and [[400 metres]] times in New York state in his junior year, with times of 21.58 seconds and 50.5 seconds, respectively.<ref name="CBS">{{Cite web |date=June 11, 2008 |title=Adam Podlesh, Maryland, NFL Draft - NFLDraftScout.com |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/historical/418811 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927073400/http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/historical/418811 |archive-date=September 27, 2013 |access-date=July 30, 2012 |publisher=CBSSports.com}}</ref> He also ran the third leg of the state title-winning [[4 x 100 metres relay]] team in 2000.

==College career==
He played [[college football]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland Terrapins]]. He spent his freshman year on the [[scout team]]. He is the only player in school history to be on the All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] team for four years. In Podlesh's 48 games played at Maryland, he punted 216 times for 9,314 yards, which ranks fifth in school history (behind Dan DeArmas, [[Dale Castro]], Russ Edwards, and Darryl Wright). His punting average of 43.1 yards ranks behind [[Brooks Barnard]] in school history. He had 83 of his attempts land inside the 20-yard line, with 35 of them landing inside the 10-yard line.

===2003 season===
As a freshman at the University of Maryland, Podlesh appeared in all 12 regular season games and the bowl game for the [[2003 Maryland Terrapins football team|Terrapins]]. On August 28, 2003, in the season opener against [[2003 Northern Illinois Huskies football team|Northern Illinois]], Podlesh had a season-high eight punts for a season-high net of 363 yards in the 20–13 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Maryland at Northern Illinois Box Score, August 28, 2003 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2003-08-28-northern-illinois.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170722144856/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2003-08-28-northern-illinois.html |archive-date=July 22, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> In the [[2004 Gator Bowl|Gator Bowl]] against [[2003 West Virginia Mountaineers football team|West Virginia]], Podlesh had two punts for 67 yards in the 41–7 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gator Bowl – West Virginia vs Maryland Box Score, January 1, 2004 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2004-01-01-maryland.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170723015226/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2004-01-01-maryland.html |archive-date=July 23, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Overall, in his freshman season, Podlesh had 53 punts for 2,241 yards for a 42.3 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Podlesh 2003 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adam-podlesh-1/gamelog/2003 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170715150855/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adam-podlesh-1/gamelog/2003 |archive-date=July 15, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref>

===2004 season===
As a sophomore, Podlesh appeared in 11 regular season games. On October 9, 2004, against [[2004 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets football team|Georgia Tech]], Podlesh had a then-career high nine punts for a then-career high 448 net yards in the 20–7 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Georgia Tech at Maryland Box Score, October 9, 2004 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2004-10-09-maryland.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170722160420/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2004-10-09-maryland.html |archive-date=July 22, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> In the following week against [[2004 NC State Wolfpack football team|NC State]], Podlesh set career highs with 11 punts for 497 net yards in the 13–3 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=North Carolina State at Maryland Box Score, October 16, 2004 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2004-10-16-maryland.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170722213528/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2004-10-16-maryland.html |archive-date=July 22, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> In the 2004 season, Podlesh had 63 punts for 2,756 yards for a 43.7 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Podlesh 2004 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adam-podlesh-1/gamelog/2004 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170715150852/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adam-podlesh-1/gamelog/2004 |archive-date=July 15, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref>

===2005 season===
As a junior, Podlesh appeared in 11 regular season games. On September 24, 2005, against [[2005 Wake Forest Demon Deacons football team|Wake Forest]], Podlesh had a season-high 298 net yards on six punts in the 22–12 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Maryland at Wake Forest Box Score, September 24, 2005 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2005-09-24-wake-forest.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170705104120/http://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2005-09-24-wake-forest.html |archive-date=July 5, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Overall, in the 2005 season, Podlesh had 44 punts for 1,918 yards for a 43.6 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Podlesh 2005 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adam-podlesh-1/gamelog/2005 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170715150853/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adam-podlesh-1/gamelog/2005 |archive-date=July 15, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> In recognition of his successful season, Podlesh was named to the ''[[Jewish Sports Review]]''’s 2005 College Football All-America Team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 23, 2006 |title=2005 College Football All-America Team |url=http://www.jewishsportsreview.com/2005AllAmerica.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131015232721/http://www.jewishsportsreview.com/2005AllAmerica.htm |archive-date=October 15, 2013 |access-date=March 14, 2013 |website=[[Jewish Sports Review]]}}</ref>

===2006 season===
Podlesh set the school record for a punter in the spring with a 4.44 time in the [[40-yard dash]] in 2006 spring training, which earned him the Iron Terp Award.<ref name=CBS/>

As a senior, Podlesh appeared in all 12 regular season games and the bowl game. On November 11, 2006, against [[2005 Miami Hurricanes football team|Miami]], Podlesh had a season-high 332 net yards on eight punts in the 14–13 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Miami at Maryland Box Score, November 11, 2006 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2006-11-11-maryland.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170722103603/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2006-11-11-maryland.html |archive-date=July 22, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> On December 29, in the [[2006 Champs Sports Bowl|Champs Sports Bowl]], Podlesh had four punts for 157 net yards in the 24–7 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Champs Sports Bowl – Purdue vs Maryland Box Score, December 29, 2006 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2006-12-29-maryland.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170712133929/http://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2006-12-29-maryland.html |archive-date=July 12, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Overall, in the 2006 season, Podlesh had 56 punts for 2,400 yards for a 42.9 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Podlesh 2006 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adam-podlesh-1/gamelog/2006 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170715150854/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adam-podlesh-1/gamelog/2006 |archive-date=July 15, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===

====2007 season====

Podlesh was selected by the Jacksonville Jaguars in the fourth round of the [[2007 NFL draft]] with the 101st overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181103015035/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |archive-date=November 3, 2018 |access-date=March 21, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In his rookie season, Podlesh appeared in all 16 regular season games and two playoff games. On September 9, in his NFL debut against the [[2007 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]], Podlesh had five punts for 211 net yards in the 13–10 loss at [[EverBank Field]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Jacksonville Jaguars – September 9th, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200709090jax.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170624061225/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200709090jax.htm |archive-date=June 24, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Against the [[2007 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], Podlesh had eight punts for a season-high 364 net yards in the 24–23 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Tampa Bay Buccaneers – October 28th, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200710280tam.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170621150456/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200710280tam.htm |archive-date=June 21, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Podlesh would make his playoff debut against the [[2007 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the [[2007–08 NFL playoffs#AFC: Jacksonville Jaguars 31, Pittsburgh Steelers 29|Wild Card Round]] of the [[2007-08 NFL playoffs|playoffs]]. In the 31–29 victory, he had four punts for 200 net yards.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=Adam Podlesh 2007 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PodlAd20/gamelog/2007 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170902205642/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PodlAd20/gamelog/2007 |archive-date=September 2, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> The next week, the Jaguars faced off against the 16–0 [[2007 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] in the [[2007–08 NFL playoffs#AFC: New England Patriots 31, Jacksonville Jaguars 20|Divisional Round]]. In the 31–20 defeat, Podlesh had one punt for 50 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Jacksonville Jaguars at New England Patriots |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200801120nwe.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180130034216/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200801120nwe.htm |archive-date=January 30, 2018 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Although this was only his rookie season, Podlesh would never appear in another playoff game.

Overall, in the 2007 season, Podlesh had 54 punts for 2,249 net yards for a 41.65 average.<ref name="auto" />

====2008 season====

On June 2, 2008, he was elected to the Rochester Jewish Sports Hall of Fame. He was participating in the Jaguars [[Training camp (National Football League)|OTA]] workouts, so his grandmother, Betty Podlesh, accepted the honor for him.<ref name="rochester_jewish_hof">{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Ryan |date=June 4, 2008 |title=Hometown honors Podlesh |url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article.aspx?id=6988 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080618191641/http://www.jaguars.com/News/Article.aspx?id=6988 |archive-date=June 18, 2008 |access-date=September 2, 2011 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref>

In the 2008 season, Podlesh appeared in 11 games. Against the [[2008 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]] in the season opener on September 7, Podlesh had six punts for 222 net yards in the 17–10 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Tennessee Titans – September 7th, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200809070oti.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180318054626/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200809070oti.htm |archive-date=March 18, 2018 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In another game with the Titans on November 16, Podlesh had 10 punts for a career-high 409 net yards in the 24–14 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Jacksonville Jaguars – November 16th, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200811160jax.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170702191954/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200811160jax.htm |archive-date=July 2, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

Overall, in the 2008 season, Podlesh had 46 punts for 1,989 yards for a 43.24 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Podlesh 2008 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PodlAd20/gamelog/2008 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160404061250/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PodlAd20/gamelog/2008/ |archive-date=April 4, 2016 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2009 season====

In the 2009 season, Podlesh appeared in all 16 regular season games. Against the [[2009 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] in the season opener on September 13, Podlesh had five punts for 189 net yards in the 14–12 loss at [[Lucas Oil Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Indianapolis Colts – September 13th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200909130clt.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170702192336/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200909130clt.htm |archive-date=July 2, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Against the [[2009 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] in Week 5, Podlesh had a season-high 371 net yards on eight punts in the 41–0 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Seattle Seahawks – October 11th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200910110sea.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170702192630/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200910110sea.htm |archive-date=July 2, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Against the [[2009 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]] in Week 13, Podlesh had three punts for 148 net yards for a season-high 49.33 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars – December 6th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200912060jax.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170630220849/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200912060jax.htm |archive-date=June 30, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

Overall, in the 2009 season, Podlesh had 72 punts for 3,017 yards for a 41.90 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Podlesh 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PodlAd20/gamelog/2009 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160404034107/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PodlAd20/gamelog/2009/ |archive-date=April 4, 2016 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2010 season====

In 2010, Podlesh was diagnosed with cancer of the [[salivary gland]], but following successful surgery he was told that [[radiation therapy]] and [[chemotherapy]] would not be required, and he returned to the field after six weeks, not missing any playing time.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sullivan |first=Bryan |date=July 22, 2011 |title=Pittsford native Podlesh excited to return to the playing field – Henrietta, NY |url=http://www.henriettapost.com/monroecountysports/x1797079449/Pittsford-native-Podlesh-excited-to-return-to-the-playing-field |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120328015340/http://www.henriettapost.com/monroecountysports/x1797079449/Pittsford-native-Podlesh-excited-to-return-to-the-playing-field |archive-date=March 28, 2012 |access-date=July 30, 2012 |website=Henrietta Post}}</ref><ref name="chicagosuntimes30Aug">{{Cite news |last=Jensen |first=Sean |date=August 30, 2011 |title=New Bear Adam Podlesh's cancer fight gives punter fresh perspective |url=http://www.suntimes.com/7373078-417/new-bear-adam-podleshs-cancer-fight-gives-punter-fresh-perspective.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121012040410/http://www.suntimes.com/7373078-417/new-bear-adam-podleshs-cancer-fight-gives-punter-fresh-perspective.html |archive-date=October 12, 2012 |access-date=September 2, 2011 |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]}}</ref>

In the 2010 season, Podlesh appeared in all 16 regular season games. Against the [[2010 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] in the season opener on September 12, Podlesh had four punts for 165 net yards in the 24–17 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denver Broncos at Jacksonville Jaguars – September 12th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201009120jax.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170702193303/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201009120jax.htm |archive-date=July 2, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Against the [[2010 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] in Week 3, Podlesh had a season-high 384 net yards on eight punts in the 28–3 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Jacksonville Jaguars – September 26th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201009260jax.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170512232848/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201009260jax.htm |archive-date=May 12, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Against the [[2010 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]] in Week 8, Podlesh had five punts for 242 net yards for a season-high 48.40 average in the 35–17 victory at [[Cowboys Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Dallas Cowboys – October 31st, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201010310dal.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171021060704/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201010310dal.htm |archive-date=October 21, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

Overall, in the 2010 season, Podlesh had 57 punts for 2,496 yards for a 43.79 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Podlesh 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PodlAd20/gamelog/2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160403211629/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PodlAd20/gamelog/2010/ |archive-date=April 3, 2016 |access-date=July 10, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===

====2011 season====
On July 29, 2011, Podlesh signed with the Chicago Bears, who had released veteran [[Brad Maynard]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sieck |first=Tim |date=July 28, 2011 |title=Bears Sign Punter Adam Podlesh |url=https://chicago.sbnation.com/chicago-bears/2011/7/28/2300506/2011-NFL-Free-Agency-Chicago-Bears |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221021135700/https://chicago.sbnation.com/chicago-bears/2011/7/28/2300506/2011-NFL-Free-Agency-Chicago-Bears |archive-date=October 21, 2022 |access-date=October 21, 2022 |website=SB Nation Chicago |language=en}}</ref>

In the 2011 season, Podlesh appeared in all 16 regular season games. Against the [[2011 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] in the season opener on September 11, Podlesh had six punts for 288 net yards in his Bears debut at [[Soldier Field]] as the Bears won 30–12.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Chicago Bears – September 11th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201109110chi.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201005014220/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201109110chi.htm |archive-date=October 5, 2020 |access-date=October 21, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Against the [[2011 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] in Week 14, Podlesh had a career-high 11 punts for a career-high 526 net yards in the 13–10 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Denver Broncos – December 11th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201112110den.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170710184508/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201112110den.htm |archive-date=July 10, 2017 |access-date=October 21, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Against the [[2011 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]] on [[Christmas Day]], Podlesh had a season high 49.00 yards per punt average in the 35–21 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers – December 25th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201112250gnb.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170829074801/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201112250gnb.htm |archive-date=August 29, 2017 |access-date=October 21, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Overall, in the 2011 season, Podlesh had 89 punts for 3,903 yards for a 43.85 average.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Podlesh 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PodlAd20/gamelog/2011 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103124931/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/P/PodlAd20/gamelog/2011 |archive-date=January 3, 2019 |access-date=October 21, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Podlesh recorded a 40.4 yard net average in the 2011 season, the best average by a Chicago Bear since [[1966 Chicago Bears season|1966]], despite injuries to special teamers [[Patrick Mannelly]], [[Brian Iwuh]], [[Kyle Adams (American football)|Kyle Adams]], and [[Anthony Walters (American football)|Anthony Walters]], as well as [[Chris Conte]], [[Major Wright]], and [[Kahlil Bell]] becoming starters, and [[Sam Hurd]] getting released. His 43.85 yard gross average was the best of his career, and was the third highest in team history, behind [[Todd Sauerbrun]]'s 44.8 in [[1996 Chicago Bears season|1996]] and [[Brad Maynard]]'s 44.2 in [[2006 Chicago Bears season|2006]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=January 5, 2012 |title=Podlesh, punt team excelled this season |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/NewsStory.asp?story_id=8547 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120108195632/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/NewsStory.asp?story_id=8547 |archive-date=January 8, 2012 |access-date=July 30, 2012 |website=Chicago Bears}}</ref>

In the 2012 season, Podlesh appeared in all 16 regular season games. Against the [[2012 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] in the season opener at home on September 9, Podlesh had five punts for 208 net yards in the 41–21 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Chicago Bears – September 9th, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201209090chi.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211200651/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201209090chi.htm |archive-date=February 11, 2022 |access-date=October 21, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 2, against the [[2012 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]], Podlesh had a season-high 46.80 yards per punt average in the 23–10 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Green Bay Packers – September 13th, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201209130gnb.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224193328/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201209130gnb.htm |archive-date=February 24, 2018 |access-date=October 21, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 12 against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], Podlesh faked the extra point, and ran it in for a two-point conversion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hendricks |first=Maggie |date=November 25, 2012 |title=Bears use special teams' trickery in win over Vikings (VIDEO) |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nfl-shutdown-corner/bears-special-teams-trickery-win-over-vikings-video-220535432--nfl.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121129083251/http://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nfl-shutdown-corner/bears-special-teams-trickery-win-over-vikings-video-220535432--nfl.html |archive-date=November 29, 2012 |access-date=November 25, 2012 |website=[[Yahoo! ====2013 season====

In the 2013 season, Podlesh appeared in all 16 regular season games. '''Adam Hayward''' (born June 23, 1984) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the sixth round of the [[2007 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Portland State Vikings football|Portland State Vikings]]. After his professional football days, he was a Firefighter/EMT in Florida.<ref>{{cite web | last=Wronka | first=Tim | title=No More 'Hand-Me-Downs' for Hillsborough County Firefighters | website=Spectrum Bay News 9 | date=2020-02-12 | url=https://baynews9.com/fl/tampa/news/2020/02/12/no-more--hand-me-downs--for-hillsborough-county-firefighters | access-date=2025-06-08}}</ref>

==Early life==
A linebacker at [[Marina High School (Huntington Beach, California)|Marina High School]], Adam was unnerved by the idea of playing the position of Safety for [[Colorado State University]],<ref name="pzpower">{{citation|last=Hopkins |first=Pz |title=Where There's a Will, There's a Way: An Interview with Adam Hayward |url=http://www.pzpower.com/column/adam-hayward-where-theres-a-will |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110314082116/http://www.pzpower.com/column/adam-hayward-where-theres-a-will |archivedate=March 14, 2011 }}</ref> He took a year off from football at Colorado to take care of some family issues.<ref name="pzpower" /> Eventually, he found his place starting as an outside linebacker for [[Portland State University]] under [[Tim Walsh (American football)|Tim Walsh]].<ref name="pzpower" />

==Professional career==

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
Hayward was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the sixth round (184th pick) of the [[2007 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-11 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
On March 10, 2014, Hayward signed a three-year deal with the [[Washington Redskins]].<ref>{{cite news|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2014/03/11/redskins-add-ilbspecial-teams-standout-adam-hayward/|title=Redskins add ILB/special teams standout Adam Hayward|first=Mike|last=Jones|date=March 11, 2014|accessdate=March 11, 2014}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve due to a [[tibial plateau fracture]] in his right leg on November 24.<ref>{{cite news|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2014/11/24/redskins-place-adam-hayward-on-ir-promote-steve-beauharnais/|title=Redskins place Adam Hayward on IR, promote Steve Beauharnais|first=Mike|last=Jones|date=November 24, 2014|accessdate=December 2, 2014}}</ref> He suffered the fracture after jumping to catch the ball during a punt in the Week 12 game against the [[San Francisco 49ers]].

Hayward tore one of his [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACLs]] in the second 2015 preseason games against the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{cite web|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/washington-commanders/post/_/id/19164/redskins-lb-adam-hayward-tears-acl-done-for-the-season|title=Redskins LB Adam Hayward tears ACL, done for the season|first=John|last=Keim|date=August 21, 2015|access-date=August 21, 2015}}</ref> On August 22, 2015, the Redskins placed him on injured reserve for the second time in a row.<ref>{{cite news|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/football-insider/wp/2015/08/22/redskins-place-hayward-on-injured-reserve-freeing-up-roster-spot/|title=Redskins place Hayward on injured reserve, freeing up roster spot|first=Liz|last=Clarke|date=August 22, 2015|accessdate=August 23, 2015}}</ref>

Hayward was released on July 22, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|work=Redskins.com|url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Release-Linebacker-Adam-Hayward/5c9abf6f-3298-497a-8879-e11a8673cf9f|title=Redskins Release Linebacker Adam Hayward|first=Stephen|last=Czarda|date=July 22, 2016|accessdate=July 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160723161819/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Release-Linebacker-Adam-Hayward/5c9abf6f-3298-497a-8879-e11a8673cf9f|archive-date=July 23, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Aaron Wallace''' (born April 17, 1967) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who played his entire career as a [[linebacker]] for the [[Oakland Raiders|Raiders franchise]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]].

Wallace attended Dallas [[Franklin D. Roosevelt High School (Dallas)]] where he was a teammate of future NFL players [[Richmond Webb]] and [[Kevin Williams (wide receiver, born 1971)|Kevin Williams]].

While at Texas A&M from 1986 to 1989, Wallace accumulated 42 sacks for his career, which still rank him 1st all-time at Texas A&M. The 42 sacks also ranked him 7th all-time in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] at the conclusion of his career and currently rank him 11th.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.fbsstatistics.com/careersacks1980.htm |title=Career Sacks Since 1980 - FBS Statistics |access-date=October 17, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612142114/http://www.fbsstatistics.com/careersacks1980.htm |archive-date=June 12, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Wallace was selected by the Raiders in the second round of the 1990 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1990 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1990/draft.htm |access-date=May 24, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Wallace played eight seasons for the Raiders, compiling 155 tackles and 21 sacks. He retired in 1999 and did some work in real estate. He later returned to Texas A&M to earn his degree in agricultural and life sciences in 2002.<ref name=WallaceADMN>{{cite news|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/colleges/texasam/stories/120608dnspohallfame.2fd6add.html|title=Three Roosevelt alumni to join Texas Black Sports Hall of Fame}}</ref>

Wallace began his coaching career at [[Sunset High School (Dallas, Texas)|Sunset High School]], where he coached the defensive line for four seasons. He then served at [[H. Grady Spruce High School]] in 2007, the last season Spruce fielded athletic teams. After Spruce's disbandment of its sports squads, he moved to [[Emmett J. Conrad High School]], though he discontinued coaching. He stopped coaching since he desired more time to see his son play football in San Diego.<ref name=WallaceADMN/> His son, [[Aaron Wallace Jr.]], played for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]] and was drafted in the 7th round of the [[2016 NFL draft]] by the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/draft.htm |access-date=2025-08-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Wallace was inducted into the Texas Black Sports Hall of Fame in 2008.<ref name=WallaceADMN/>

'''Adam Koets''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|k|oʊ|t|s}}; born January 7, 1984) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive tackle]] for the [[New York Giants]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He was selected by the Giants in the sixth round of the [[2007 NFL draft]].  He played [[college football]] for the [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State Beavers]].

==Early life==
Koets was born in Santa Ana, California to parents Russell and Helen Koets.  He has one older brother, Jeff and an older sister, Amber.  Koets attended [[Foothill High School (Santa Ana, California)|Foothill High School]] in [[North Tustin, California]].  Koets [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] three years in [[high school football|football]].  He started three years as a [[defensive end]] and his senior season as a left tackle on offense.  He was chosen as a first-team All-Century League on offense his final season and a three-time all-league selection on defense.  Koets was the Century League Defensive Lineman of the Year twice and second-team All-Orange County and first-team All-CIF Division VI on offense as a senior.  In his high school career, he had 229 tackles and 16 quarterback sacks.  He graduated from Foothill High in 2002.

==College career==
Koets attended [[Oregon State University]] where he played [[offensive tackle]].  After redshirting in 2002, Koets played in five games in 2003 as a redshirt freshman.  In 2004, he started all 12 games.  As a junior in 2005, Koets started all 11 games at left tackle.  His play assisted Beaver running back [[Yvenson Bernard]] to rank ninth in the nation with a 120.1 yards per game average and quarterback [[Matt Moore (American football)|Matt Moore]] to finish second in the Pac-10 for yards per game passing at 271.1 yards per game.  In his senior year in 2006, Koets was a second-team All [[Pac-10 Conference]] selection after helping the team to average 360.6 yards per game.  He started all 13 games his senior season.  In his time with Oregon State, he was a three-time Academic All-Pac-10 Conference selection.  He graduated with a major in International Business and a minor in German.

==Professional career==
Koets was selected by the Giants in the sixth round of the [[2007 NFL draft]] with the 189th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-11 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During his four-year career, he played eleven games, starting four.<ref>{{cite web |title=Adam Koets, OT |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/adamkoets/2495656/profile |website=nfl.com |publisher=NFL Productions, LLC. |access-date=10 November 2019}}</ref> In the 2007 postseason, he started the [[2007–08 NFL playoffs]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Wild Card - New York Giants at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - January 6th, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200801060tam.htm |website=Pro-football-Reference.com |access-date=10 November 2019}}</ref>

He was released from the Physically Unable to Perform list on November 8, 2011.<ref>{{Citation |date=January 13, 2011 |title=NFL Transactions Report |url=http://www.nfl.com/transactions?transactionMonth=11&transactionYear=2011&transactionTeamAbbr=NYG&prevTransactionMonth=11&prevTransactionYear=2011&prevTransactionTeamAbbr=}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Koets is a thrill seeker, enjoying sky diving, [[bungee jumping]], surfing and other related extreme sports.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cfdsny.org/htmlweb/news_11_telethon_koets.html |title=Giants Tackle Adam Koets at 2011 Telethon! |access-date=May 31, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105234911/http://www.cfdsny.org/htmlweb/news_11_telethon_koets.html |archive-date=November 5, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
Koets is also an accomplished singer and has appeared with the Grove Valve Orchestra, a band led by food industry magnate, Gary Erickson.

'''Aaron Williams''' (born April 23, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] and was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the second round of the [[2011 NFL draft]].

== Early life ==
Williams attended [[McNeil High School]] in [[Austin, Texas]]. He was considered the top [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'' and the second best [[cornerback]] recruit by ''[[Scout.com]]'' in 2008.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/rankings/rank-1833;_ylt=AgJvYeubyPaa4EyqUIdxpq5GPZB4 Rivals.com safeties 2008 rankings]</ref><ref>[http://recruiting.scout.com/a.z?s=73&p=9&c=4&pid=30&yr=2008 Scout.com Scout.com cornerback 2008 rankings]</ref> He was selected 1st team All-State by [[Dave Campbell's Texas Football|Dave Campbell Texas Football magazine]] and was also named to the 2008 Parade All-American team.  Williams was named an outstanding performer at the 2007 Army National Combine which led to him being selected to the 2008 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]] game. He was also a two-year letterman in [[baseball]] and [[track & field]]. He chose Texas over offers from [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor]] and [[USC Trojans football|USC]].

== College career ==
As a freshman in 2008, Williams started one of 13 games at cornerback, recording 13 tackles and an [[interception]] which was returned 81 yards for a [[touchdown]]. As a sophomore in 2009, he played in 13 games, missing one due to an injury, and recorded 31 tackles, two [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] and three interceptions. As a junior in 2010, he started 11 games, missing two due to an injury, and recorded 45 tackles, one quarterback sack, and two forced fumbles.

== Professional career ==
[[File:Aaron Williams (American football).JPG|thumb|Williams with the Bills in 2011]]
Williams was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] as the second pick of the second round (no. 34 overall) in the [[2011 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |title=2011 NFL Draft Listing |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=2019-02-26}}</ref>

Following an up and down first two seasons at [[cornerback]], Williams was moved to [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]] for the [[2013 NFL season|2013 season]].

On March 5, 2014, Williams signed a four-year, $26 million extension with the Bills.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bills sign Aaron Williams to a multi-year extension|url=http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-2/Bills-sign-Aaron-Williams-to-a-multi-year-extension/3849610d-2f37-4130-ba69-9a248350d441|author=Brown, Chris|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=March 5, 2014|access-date=March 5, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140323152610/http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-2/Bills-sign-Aaron-Williams-to-a-multi-year-extension/3849610d-2f37-4130-ba69-9a248350d441|archive-date=March 23, 2014|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

In 2015, Williams was injured in a Week 2 game against the [[New England Patriots]] while attempting a flying goal line tackle on [[Julian Edelman]]. He was completely motionless on the turf, and was taken off the field in an ambulance. Early reports stated he suffered a neck injury.

In 2016, during a Week 3 game against the [[Arizona Cardinals]], Williams scored his first NFL touchdown, returning a botched field goal attempt for the score.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.espn.com/nfl/game?gameId=400874558|title = Bills bounce back with 33-18 win over Cardinals|website=ESPN.com|date=September 25, 2016}}</ref> In Week 7, Williams suffered another serious neck injury after a hit by [[Miami Dolphins]] [[wide receiver]] [[Jarvis Landry]]. He was placed on injured reserve on November 1, 2016, effectively ending his season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bills sign Percy Harvin in effort to bolster receiver position|url=http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/Bills-sign-Percy-Harvin-in-effort-to-bolster-receiver-position/af216bef-8820-4438-a5a2-c1d0973b41fb|author=Brown, Chris|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=November 1, 2016|access-date=November 1, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170728204532/http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/Bills-sign-Percy-Harvin-in-effort-to-bolster-receiver-position/af216bef-8820-4438-a5a2-c1d0973b41fb|archive-date=July 28, 2017|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

On March 9, 2017, Williams was released by the Bills.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bills release veteran safety Aaron Williams|url=http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/Bills-release-veteran-safety-Aaron-Williams/e80c18a4-6956-4fad-aacb-5085ec170e00|author=Brown, Chris|website=BuffaloBills.com|date=March 9, 2017|access-date=March 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170311153738/http://www.buffalobills.com/news/article-1/Bills-release-veteran-safety-Aaron-Williams/e80c18a4-6956-4fad-aacb-5085ec170e00|archive-date=March 11, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On January 31, 2018, Williams announced his retirement from the NFL after six seasons in Buffalo.<ref>{{cite web|title=To Buffalo|url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/aaron-williams-bills-retirement/|author=Williams, Aaron|website=ThePlayersTribune.com|date=January 31, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Former Bills DB Aaron Williams announces retirement|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/former-bills-db-aaron-williams-announces-retirement-0ap3000000912804|author=Lewis, Edward|website=NFL.com|date=January 31, 2018}}</ref> His retirement came after multiple head and neck injuries throughout his career, citing it was the main concern of other teams not signing him after workouts in 2017, including the Jaguars, Texans, and Chiefs.

'''Adam Bighill''' (born October 16, 1988) is a former American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He most recently played for the [[Calgary Stampeders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He is a three-time [[Grey Cup]] champion, winning with the [[BC Lions]] in [[99th Grey Cup|2011]] and twice more with the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] in [[107th Grey Cup|2019]] and [[108th Grey Cup|2021]]. He is a three-time winner of the [[CFL's Most Outstanding Defensive Player Award]] and is a six-time CFL All-Star and eight-time [[CFL West]] All-Star. He also spent time with the [[New Orleans Saints]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Central Washington Wildcats football|Central Washington Wildcats]].

==Professional career==
=== BC Lions ===
After going undrafted in the [[2011 NFL draft]], Bighill signed as a [[free agent]] with the [[BC Lions]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on May 31, 2011.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://www.bclions.com/roster/show/id/4053|title=Roster - B.C. Lions|work=BC Lions|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111130020357/http://www.bclions.com/roster/show/id/4053|archive-date=2011-11-30|url-status=dead}}</ref> Bighill had an impressive rookie season, playing an increased role as the season progressed. He played in 12 games, including the final seven regular season games, and the West Final and Grey Cup games. He led the club, and was ranked fourth overall in the CFL, with 22 special team tackles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/statistics/league/stat/Sptackles/year/2011/type/reg|title=Special Teams Tackles 2011 - Statistics - CFL.ca - Official Site of the Canadian Football League|work=CFL.ca|access-date=2017-08-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150316183300/http://cfl.ca/statistics/league/stat/Sptackles/year/2011/type/reg|archive-date=2015-03-16|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Bighill began the [[2012 CFL season]] by replacing [[Solomon Elimimian]] at middle linebacker for the Lions, after Elimimian was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bclions.com/article/ready-for-the-real-deal|title=Ready for the real deal|work=BC Lions|access-date=2012-07-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120729033731/http://www.bclions.com/article/ready-for-the-real-deal|archive-date=2012-07-29|url-status=dead}}</ref> After assuming the starting linebacker role, Bighill went on to amass 104 tackles (2nd most in the CFL) and 4 interceptions. Elimimian returned to the Lions midway through the season, but Bighill retained all of the playing time. He was named both a CFL West All-Star and a CFL All-Star for the 2012 season.

Bighill and Elimimian both returned to the Lions linebacker core for the [[2013 CFL season]]. Bighill suffered a sprained ankle and missed Week 3 and 4.<ref>[https://theprovince.com/sports/football/bc-lions/break+Bighill+just+break+heal/8625933/story.html Sprained ankle, 2013 CFL season]{{dead link|date=October 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He played in the 16 other regular season games, and the Lions' lone playoff game. Bighill put together a strong 2013 season, accumulating 92 tackles, 12 special teams tackles, 9 sacks, 1 interception and 3 fumble recoveries (one of which he returned for a touchdown; his first of his career). In [[2014 CFL season|2014]], Bighill played in all but one of the 18 regular season games as well as one playoff game. He totalled 77 tackles, 12 special teams tackles, 6 sacks, 1 interception, and 1 fumble recovery. Following the season, Bighill's linebacker teammate, Solomon Elimimian, was named the leagues MOP, and both of them signed 3-year contract extensions on the same day.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.tsn.ca/lions-extend-lbs-elimimian-bighill-1.203968|title = Lions extend LBs Elimimian, Bighill|website = TSN}}</ref>

In Bighill's fifth season with the Lions he played in all but one game of the regular season, contributing a league leading 117 tackles. Following the season, Bighill was named the [[CFL's Most Outstanding Defensive Player Award|CFL's Top Defensive Player]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Adam Bighill named CFL's top defensive player {{!}} or-politics.comor-politics.com |url=http://or-politics.com/uncategorized/adam-bighill-named-cfls-top-defensive-player/185980/ |website=or-politics.com |access-date=2015-11-27 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208130115/http://or-politics.com/uncategorized/adam-bighill-named-cfls-top-defensive-player/185980/ |archive-date=2015-12-08 }}</ref> Bighill continued his dominant play in the [[2016 CFL season|2016 season]] finishing 3rd in the league in tackles and earning his fourth CFL All-Star award in the past five seasons. On December 9, 2016, the BC Lions granted Bighill a release as per the agreements in his contract which allows him to pursue an NFL contract up until January 27, 2017. If he is unable to sign an NFL contract by that date he will be back under contract with the BC Lions through the 2018 CFL season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2016/12/09/lions-release-bighill-to-pursue-opportunities-down-south/|title=Lions grant Bighill release to pursue opportunities down south|date=2016-12-09|website=CFL.ca|access-date=2016-12-09}}</ref>  Through six CFL seasons Bighill amassed 489 defensive tackles, 69 special teams tackles, 33 sacks, 8 interceptions, 8 forced fumbles and 1 defensive touchdown.

Bighill had a workout with the New Orleans Saints on December 13, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theadvocate.com/new_orleans/sports/saints/article_49e13ad2-d2f3-11e6-81a8-a734f795bceb.html|title=Saints continue to mine CFL ranks, sign linebacker, defensive back|first=NICK|last=UNDERHILL|website=The Advocate}}</ref>

=== New Orleans Saints ===
Bighill signed a future/reserve contract with the [[New Orleans Saints]] on January 4, 2017.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tsn.ca/saints-sign-cfl-s-bighill-1.644076|title=Saints sign CFL's Bighill|date=January 4, 2017|newspaper=TSN|access-date=January 5, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints sign 2 defensive players from CFL|url=http://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2017/01/saints_sign_2_from_cfl.html#incart_most-read_saints_article|author=Dabe, Christopher|website=NOLA.com|date=January 4, 2017}}</ref> Bighill drew strongly positive attention for his performance during the Saints training camp and preseason. He was waived on September 2, and was signed to the Saints' practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=New Orleans Saints make 37 roster
