=== Winnipeg Blue Bombers ===
Bighill signed a one-year deal with the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] on May 19, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bombers sign four-time CFL All-Star linebacker Adam Bighill|url=https://www.bluebombers.com/2018/05/19/bombers-sign-adam-bighill/|website=bluebombers.com|date=May 19, 2018}}</ref> Bighill finished the 2018 season as the Blue Bomber's nominee for Most Outstanding Player,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2018/10/31/cfl-announces-2018-team-award-winners/|title=CFL announces 2018 team award winners|date=31 October 2018}}</ref> was named to the CFL All-Star team,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2018/11/07/star-power-2018-cfl-divisional-stars-announced/|title=Star Power: 2018 CFL Divisional All-Stars announced|date=7 November 2018}}</ref> and was ultimately named the [[CFL's Most Outstanding Defensive Player Award|CFL's Most Outstanding Defensive Player]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2018/11/22/adam-bighill-named-outstanding-defensive-player/|title=Adam Bighill named Most Outstanding Defensive Player - CFL.ca|date=2018-11-22|work=CFL.ca|access-date=2018-11-23|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="2018 allstars">{{cite web|title=Stars aligned: 2018 CFL All-Stars unveiled|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2018/12/04/stars-aligned-2018-cfl-stars-unveiled/|publisher=[[Canadian Football League]]|access-date=2018-12-04}}</ref> The Blue Bombers signed Bighill to a 3-year $750,000 contract extension in January 2019, making him the highest paid defensive player in the CFL.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://3downnation.com/2019/01/15/bombers-make-adam-bighill-the-highest-paid-defensive-player-in-the-cfl/|title=Bombers make Adam Bighill the highest paid defensive player in the CFL - 3DownNation|first=Justin|last=Dunk}}</ref> Bighill helped lead the defence for the Bombers as they defeated Hamilton 33–12 in the [[107th Grey Cup]], the game saw Bighill recover a fumble which led to an [[Andrew Harris (Canadian football)|Andrew Harris]] touchdown. After the win Bighill said that "I've packed too many garbage bags. I only play this game to win championships. We're bringing it home to Winnipeg, it doesn't get any better than that."<ref>{{cite news |title=Harris leads Winnipeg Blue Bombers to first Grey Cup win since 1990 |author=Dan Ralph |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/windsor/article/harris-leads-winnipeg-blue-bombers-to-first-grey-cup-win-since-1990/ |website=[[CTV News]] |publisher=[[Canadian Press]] |date=25 November 2019}}</ref>

The Bombers were set to defend their title during the [[2020 CFL season]] although it was cancelled because of the ongoing pandemic. Bighill was scheduled to make $265,000 in the following season, but he took a $145,000 pay cut to stay with the Bombers and help the team in a league that was troubled financially by the pandemic.<ref>{{cite web |title= Pay cut a massive gash: Bombers' Bighill takes $145K contract hit |author= Jason Bell |url= https://www.winnipegfreepress.com/sports/football/bombers/pay-cut-a-massive-gash-573647622.html |website= [[Winnipeg Free Press]] |date= January 22, 2021}}</ref> Bighill would go on to lead an excellent Bombers' defence that would lead the league in yards and points allowed. He had an acrobatic interception against [[Cody Fajardo]] during the 2021 [[Banjo Bowl]].<ref>{{cite web |title= Cody Fajardo still can’t believe how Adam Bighill intercepted him during the Banjo Bowl |author= John Hodge |url= https://3downnation.com/2021/09/23/cody-fajardo-still-cant-believe-how-adam-bighill-intercepted-him-during-the-banjo-bowl/ |website=3DownNation |date= September 23, 2021}}</ref> Bighill would finish the season with 70 tackles, two sacks, and two interceptions. His incredible season would result in him being announced the [[CFL Most Outstanding Defensive Player Award|CFL's Most Outstanding Defensive Player]] for 2021, as well as a CFL All-Star.<ref>{{Cite news |date=December 10, 2021 |title=Winnipeg Blue Bombers linebacker Adam Bighill is CFL’s outstanding defensive player |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/football/article-winnipeg-blue-bombers-linebacker-adam-bighill-is-cfls-outstanding/ |access-date=2025-06-21 |work=[[The Globe and Mail]]|agency=[[The Canadian Press]]}}</ref> Bighill and the Bombers defeated the Saskatchewan Roughriders for the third time that season in the CFL West Division Final, as they would go on to their second Grey Cup game in a row. In the [[108th Grey Cup|2021 Grey Cup]] the Bombers trailed Hamilton late in the fourth quarter by a score of 22-10 but would rally to go on and win 33–25 in overtime for their second Grey Cup in a row. This was Bighill's third Grey Cup title. Following the season, on January 20, 2022, Bighill and the Blue Bombers agreed to a one-year contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web|author=TSN ca Staff|date=2022-01-20|title=Bombers extend Most Outstanding Defensive Player Bighill - TSN.ca|url=https://www.tsn.ca/winnipeg-blue-bombers-adam-bighill-cfl-1.1748193|access-date=2022-01-20|website=TSN|language=en}}</ref>

Bighill was named a CFL West All-Star for the eighth time in his career following the [[2022 Winnipeg Blue Bombers season|2022 season]] in which the Blue Bombers advanced to the Grey Cup final for the third consecutive season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-02 |title=Updated list of 2022 CFL Division All-Stars |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2022/11/02/updated-list-of-2022-cfl-division-all-stars/ |access-date=2022-11-29 |website=CFL.ca |language=en}}</ref> He had one defensive tackle in the [[109th Grey Cup]], but the Blue Bombers were defeated by the [[Toronto Argonauts]]. On November 29, 2022, the Bombers announced that Bighill had re-signed with the club on a new two-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |author=3Down Staff |date=2022-11-29 |title=Winnipeg Blue Bombers sign linebacker Adam Bighill to two-year contract extension |url=https://3downnation.com/2022/11/29/winnipeg-blue-bombers-sign-linebacker-adam-bighill-to-two-year-contract-extension/ |access-date=2022-11-29 |website=3DownNation |language=en-US}}</ref>

In [[2023 Winnipeg Blue Bombers season|2023]], Bighill played and started in 17 regular season games where he had 74 defensive tackles, four sacks, and one interception. He played in his fourth straight Grey Cup game, but the Blue Bombers lost to the [[Montreal Alouettes]].<ref name=110GC>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cfl.ca/games/6391/montreal-alouettes-vs-winnipeg-blue%20bombers/ |title=110th Grey Cup |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 11, 2024}}</ref> In the [[2024 Winnipeg Blue Bombers season|2024 season]], he played in the first ten games of the season where he had 48 defensive tackles and one sack before an injury sidelined him for the remainder of the season.<ref name=movingon>{{Cite web |url=https://3downnation.com/2025/01/24/bombers-moving-on-from-veteran-lb-adam-bighill-report/ |title=Winnipeg Blue Bombers moving on from veteran LB Adam Bighill: report |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |date=January 24, 2025}}</ref> In January 2025, Bighill indicated that the Blue Bombers would not be offering him a new contract for the 2025 season. He became a [[free agent]] upon the expiry of his contract on February 11, 2025.<ref name=2025T>{{Cite news |url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/2025/ |title=Transactions – Football Player Trades and Signings |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 20, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.cfl.ca/fa25/ |title=Official 2025 Free Agent Tracker |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 20, 2025}}</ref>

===Calgary Stampeders===
On June 22, 2025, it was announced that Bighill had signed a practice roster agreement with the [[Calgary Stampeders]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.stampeders.com/2025/06/22/stamps-add-veteran-adam-bighill/ |title=Stamps Add Veteran Adam Bighill |publisher=[[Calgary Stampeders]] |date=June 22, 2025}}</ref> He played in six regular season games in [[2025 Calgary Stampeders season|2025]] where he had 12 defensive tackles and one special teams tackle. He became a [[free agent]] upon the expiry of his contract on February 10, 2026.<ref name=2026T>{{Cite news |url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/2026/ |title=Transactions – Football Player Trades and Signings |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 14, 2026}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On April 21, 2026, Bighill signed a one-day contract with the Winnipeg Blue Bombers to officially retire with the team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Adam Bighill signs one-day contract to retire as a Blue Bomber |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2026/04/20/adam-bighill-signs-one-day-contract-to-retire-as-a-blue-bomber/ |website=CFL.ca |access-date=22 April 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Bighill was born with a bilateral [[Cleft lip and cleft palate|cleft lip and palate]]. He is President of the Canadian charity Making Faces, a charity dedicated to helping people cope with facial differences.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.thestar.com/life/2015/11/15/all-star-cfl-linebacker-adam-bighill-helps-others-with-facial-differences.html | title=All-star CFL linebacker Adam Bighill helps others with facial differences | work=thestar.com | date= November 15, 2015}}</ref> His son Beau was also born with a bilateral cleft lip. After [[Wendy Williams]] mocked [[Joaquin Phoenix]] on her show in 2020 because of his cleft lip, Bighill relentlessly called her out and requested an apology. Williams did end up making an apology to Bighill on Twitter, as well as making two donations to cleft related charities and wished his son Beau good luck on his upcoming surgery.<ref>{{cite news |title=U.S. TV host apologizes for cleft lip joke after pressure from Blue Bomber |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/manitoba/wendy-williams-bighill-apology-1.5428855 |website=[[CBC News]] |date=January 16, 2020}}</ref>

'''Adam Gettis''' (born December 9, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]] and was selected by the [[Washington Redskins]] in the fifth round of the [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|work=Redskins.com|last=Tinsman|first=Brian|title=Redskins Sign Draft Pick Adam Gettis|url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Draft-Pick-Adam-Gettis/47555e35-7ac7-4336-b387-b602eaf240b5|date=May 5, 2012|accessdate=May 22, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120508052711/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Sign-Draft-Pick-Adam-Gettis/47555e35-7ac7-4336-b387-b602eaf240b5|archive-date=May 8, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Early life==
From 2004 to 2006, Gettis played [[high school football]] for the [[Lincoln-Way East High School|Lincoln-Way East Griffins]] as a starter.  In 2005, Gettis and the Griffins went on to win the Class 8A State Championship in Illinois.

Gettis was signed from the practice squad of the Steelers to the active roster of the [[New York Giants]] on December 16, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|work=Giants.com|url=https://www.giants.com/news/5-things-you-need-to-know-about-ol-adam-gettis-14595504|title=5 things you need to know about OL Adam Gettis|first=Dan|last=Salomone|accessdate=December 16, 2014}}</ref> On September 5, 2015, he was waived by the Giants.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-53-man-roster/d90c09c7-4a11-4260-b545-8dd3a1fa0671 |title=New York Giants announce 53-man roster |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 5, 2015 |website=Giants.com |accessdate=September 7, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925072219/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-53-man-roster/d90c09c7-4a11-4260-b545-8dd3a1fa0671 |archive-date=September 25, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On September 6, 2015, he was signed to the Giants' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-sign-six-players-to-practice-squad-15822298 |title=Giants sign six players to practice squad |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 6, 2015 |website=Giants.com |accessdate=September 7, 2015}}</ref> On October 15, 2015, Gettis was released by the Giants.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/DB-Brandon-McGee-Tackle-Xavier-Proctor-added-to-Practice-Squad/393866ca-dfe3-46f3-9338-0d1f83229fd9 |title=DB Brandon McGee, Tackle Xavier Proctor added to Practice Squad |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=October 15, 2015 |website=Giants.com |accessdate=December 6, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151207040633/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/DB-Brandon-McGee-Tackle-Xavier-Proctor-added-to-Practice-Squad/393866ca-dfe3-46f3-9338-0d1f83229fd9 |archivedate=December 7, 2015 }}</ref> On October 21, 2015, he was re-signed to the practice squad. On November 4, 2015, Gettis was released by the Giants.

===Oakland Raiders===
On November 17, 2015, Gettis was signed to the [[Oakland Raiders]]' practice squad.

===New York Giants (second stint)===
On December 1, 2015, Gettis re-signed with the Giants.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Raanan|first1=Jordan|title=Giants signing offensive lineman Adam Gettis off Oakland Raiders practice squad, per source|url=http://www.nj.com/giants/index.ssf/2015/11/giants_claim_offensive_lineman_adam_gettis_from_ra.html|website=NJ.com|accessdate=December 2, 2015}}</ref> On September 3, 2016, he was released by the Giants and was signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Giants announce 20 roster moves|url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-20-roster-moves/d7b93d76-3186-40dc-b759-c622015e0159|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825063500/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-20-roster-moves/d7b93d76-3186-40dc-b759-c622015e0159|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 25, 2017|last=Eisen |first=Michael|website=Giants.com|date=September 3, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Giants announce practice squad; claim DT Robert Thomas|url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-announce-practice-squad-claim-DT-Robert-Thomas/e8402e2e-7f9b-4c94-95db-b9d10f79333e|last=Eisen|first=Michael|website=Giants.com|access-date=September 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909053715/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-announce-practice-squad-claim-DT-Robert-Thomas/e8402e2e-7f9b-4c94-95db-b9d10f79333e|archive-date=September 9, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on November 9, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Darian Thompson placed on IR; OL Adam Gettis signed|url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Darian-Thompson-placed-on-IR-OL-Adam-Gettis-signed/57683e6d-01b4-4be2-ba10-3297a7610eb1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170814225653/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Darian-Thompson-placed-on-IR-OL-Adam-Gettis-signed/57683e6d-01b4-4be2-ba10-3297a7610eb1|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 14, 2017|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=November 9, 2016}}</ref> He was waived by the Giants on December 10, 2016, and was re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=RB Shane Vereen activated from IR; Adam Gettis waived|url=https://www.giants.com/news/rb-shane-vereen-activated-from-ir-adam-gettis-waived-18240742|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=December 10, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Giants sign Adam Gettis to practice squad, terminate contracts of two others|url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2016/12/14/new-york-giants-sign-adam-gettis-practice-squad-other-transactions/|author=Benton, Dan|date=December 14, 2016}}</ref>

Gettis signed a reserve/future contract with the Giants on January 12, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants' roster moves: Twelve now signed to reserve/futures contracts|url=https://www.bigblueview.com/2017/1/12/14250808/ny-giants-roster-moves-reserve-futures-contracts-dam-gettis-ryan-murphy-jon-halapio-michael-bowie|author=Valentine, Ed|website=BigBlueView.com|date=January 12, 2017}}</ref> On August 28, 2017, Gettis was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants Place G Adam Gettis On Injured Reserve|url=https://nfltraderumors.co/giants-place-g-adam-gettis-injured-reserve/|author=Bouda, Nate|date=August 28, 2017}}</ref> He was released with a settlement on November 16, 2017.

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On December 20, 2017, Gettis signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Standout Rookies Among Five Bucs Headed to IR|url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Standout-Rookies-Among-Five-Bucs-Headed-to-IR/b5203974-8b43-4612-a385-24deb30cb4e4|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=December 20, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223235108/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Standout-Rookies-Among-Five-Bucs-Headed-to-IR/b5203974-8b43-4612-a385-24deb30cb4e4|archivedate=December 23, 2017}}</ref> On March 26, 2018, Gettis re-signed with the Buccaneers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Re-Sign Adam Gettis|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-re-sign-adam-gettis-20489313|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=March 26, 2018}}</ref> On September 11, 2018, Gettis was released by the Buccaneers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Add CB Marcus Williams, Release G Adam Gettis|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-add-cb-marcus-williams-release-g-adam-gettis|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=September 11, 2018}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On April 3, 2019, Gettis signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons sign Adam Gettis to one-year contract|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-sign-adam-gettis-to-one-year-contract|author=McFadden, Will|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=April 3, 2019}}</ref> He was released on August 31, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons 2019 roster announced|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-2019-roster-announced|author=McFadden, Will|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=August 31, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Gettis is the cousin of [[wide receiver]] [[David Gettis]], who was drafted in sixth round of the [[2010 NFL draft]] by the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite web|work=Redskins.com|url=http://blog.redskins.com/2014/01/07/david-gettis-a-familiar-target-for-rgiii/|title=David Gettis A Familiar Target For RGIII|first=Gabe|last=Hiatt|date=January 7, 2014|accessdate=January 8, 2014}}</ref>

He married Dionna Taylor in 2014, in Chicago, Illinois.

'''Tracy Lavon '''"'''Ace'''"''' Sanders''' (born November 11, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the fourth round of the [[2013 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]].

==Early life==
Sanders was born in [[Palmetto, Florida]]. He played [[high school football]] for [[Manatee High School]] in [[Bradenton]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ace Sanders, Manatee, Wide Receiver |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Ace-Sanders-2715/high-school-7499/ |access-date=September 25, 2019 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He is the son of former [[Florida State Seminoles]] [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]] Tracy Sanders.<ref>{{cite web | last=Anderson | first=Chris | title=Sanders looking for a repeat | website=Sarasota Herald-Tribune | date=December 9, 2009 | url=https://www.heraldtribune.com/story/news/2009/12/09/sanders-looking-for-a-repeat/28909331007/ | access-date=June 24, 2026}}</ref>

In addition to football, Sanders also ran [[track and field]]. He placed second in the [[100 meters]] at the 2010 FHSAA 3A District 11 Championships, setting a career-best time of 10.98 seconds.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FHSAA 3A District 11 - Complete Results (Raw) |url=https://fl.milesplit.com/meets/71087-fhsaa-3a-district-11/results/119701/raw |access-date=September 25, 2019 |website=flrunners.com |language=en}}</ref> He also competed in the [[long jump]], he had a career-best jump of 6.95 meters.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Draft 2013 Multi-Sport Breakdown |url=http://footballtalentadvisors.com/blog/2013/04/ |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140810142032/http://footballtalentadvisors.com/blog/2013/04/ |archive-date=August 10, 2014 |access-date=August 31, 2016 |website=Football Talent Advisors}}</ref>

==College career==
Sanders received an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of South Carolina]], where he played for coach [[Steve Spurrier]]'s [[South Carolina Gamecocks football]] team from 2010 to 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ace Sanders College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/ace-sanders-1.html |access-date=2025-03-02 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> As a junior in 2012, he was a first-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) selection as a kick returner, and was named SEC Special Teams Player of the Year. In the [[2013 Outback Bowl]] against the [[2012 Michigan Wolverines football team|Michigan Wolverines]], he caught a career-best nine passes for 92 yards and two touchdowns, scored on a 63-yard punt return, and was named the game's most valuable player (MVP).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Outback Bowl - South Carolina vs Michigan Box Score, January 1, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-01-01-michigan.html |access-date=September 25, 2019 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==

The [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] chose Sanders in the fourth round, with the 101st overall pick, of the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |access-date=September 25, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He registered his first career reception in Week 1 against the [[2013 Kansas City Chiefs|Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Jacksonville Jaguars - September 8th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201309080jax.htm |access-date=September 25, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> His first career punt return came in Week 4 against the [[2013 Indianapolis Colts|Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars - September 29th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201309290jax.htm |access-date=September 25, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On December 5, 2013, in a ''[[Thursday Night Football]]'' game against the [[2013 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]], Sanders threw a 21-yard touchdown pass to running back [[Jordan Todman]] on a trick screen play. The Jaguars went on to win the game, 27–20.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Jacksonville Jaguars - December 5th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201312050jax.htm |access-date=September 25, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On December 15, he scored his first touchdown reception against the [[2013 Buffalo Bills|Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Buffalo Bills at Jacksonville Jaguars - December 15th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201312150jax.htm |access-date=September 25, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Sanders finished his rookie season with 484 receiving yards on 51 catches with one touchdown, one pass for 21 yards and a touchdown, three kick returns for 140 yards, 25 for 140 yards on punt returns (with 16 fair catches) all in 15 out of the 16 regular season games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ace Sanders 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SandAc00/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=September 25, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Sanders was suspended for the first four games of the 2014 season for violating the NFL's substance abuse policy.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-07-24 |title=NFL suspends Jaguars WR Sanders 4 games |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/11256064/nfl-suspends-jacksonville-jaguars-receiver-ace-sanders-4-games |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref> He was re-activated on October 4, 2014, ahead of the Jaguars' Week 5 matchup against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oehser |first=John |date=October 4, 2014 |title=Saturday roster moves: WR Ace Sanders moved to 53-man roster |url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Saturday-roster-moves-WR-Ace-Sanders-moved-to-53-man-roster/439cf893-7bd1-49b6-94a9-66a41fdc4fb8 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006052225/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Saturday-roster-moves-WR-Ace-Sanders-moved-to-53-man-roster/439cf893-7bd1-49b6-94a9-66a41fdc4fb8 |archive-date=October 6, 2014 |access-date=October 4, 2014 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> Overall, he had six receptions for 55 yards in the 2014 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ace Sanders 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SandAc00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=September 25, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On July 17, 2015, Sanders was waived by the Jaguars.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-07-17 |title=Jaguars release WR Ace Sanders |url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nfl&id=13274910 |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>

'''Abry Jones''' (born September 8, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] for eight seasons in [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed as an undrafted free agent by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] in 2013 and played his entire career with the team.<ref name="l158">{{cite web | title=Jags unveil 22 undrafted free agents | website=NBC Sports | date=2013-04-28 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/jags-unveil-22-undrafted-free-agents | access-date=2024-12-29}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]].

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Following the [[2013 NFL draft]], Jones was signed by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] as an undrafted free agent.<ref name="x723">{{cite web | title=Jaguars Notebook: Undrafted rookie Abry Jones finds a home | website=Florida Times-Union | date=2013-09-03 | url=https://www.jacksonville.com/story/sports/nfl/2013/09/03/jaguars-notebook-undrafted-rookie-abry-jones-finds-home/15817612007/ | access-date=2024-12-17}}</ref> He made the team's 53-man roster on August 30, 2013.<ref name="k937">{{cite web | last=O'Halloran | first=Ryan | title=Jaguars slash roster, cut 21 | website=St. Augustine Record | date=2013-09-01 | url=https://www.staugustine.com/story/sports/pro/2013/09/01/jaguars-slash-roster-cut-21/16137458007/ | access-date=2024-12-17}}</ref> Jones made his NFL debut on October 6, 2013, against the [[2013 St. Louis Rams season|St. Louis Rams]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Jacksonville Jaguars: Abry Jones|url = http://www.jaguars.com/team/roster/Abry-Jones/81d47494-ec12-4db0-b455-b8a188f0d0a3|website = www.jaguars.com|access-date = January 3, 2016}}</ref> On October 20, 2013, Jones made his first career tackle against the [[2013 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Chargers vs. Jaguars - Box Score - October 20, 2013 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=331020030|website = ESPN.com|access-date = January 3, 2016}}</ref> On December 22, 2013, Jones recorded his first career sack and a season high four tackles against the [[2013 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Titans vs. Jaguars - Box Score - December 22, 2013 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=331222030|website = ESPN.com|access-date = January 3, 2016}}</ref>

On October 5, 2014, Jones recorded a career-high two sacks including his first career forced fumble against the [[2014 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Steelers vs. Jaguars - Play-By-Play - October 5, 2014 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/playbyplay?gameId=400554243|website = ESPN.com|access-date = January 2, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = Steelers vs. Jaguars - Box Score - October 5, 2014 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=400554243|website = ESPN.com|access-date = January 2, 2016}}</ref> On December 18, 2014, Jones made his first career start and recorded a career high five tackles against the [[2014 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Titans vs. Jaguars - Box Score - December 18, 2014 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=400554356|website = ESPN.com|access-date = January 3, 2016}}</ref> In the 2014 season at the time, Jones recorded a career-best 39 tackles, three sacks, four tackles for loss, and one forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abry Jones 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JoneAb00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=2024-12-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On October 4, 2015, Jones recorded his first career [[fumble recovery]] against the [[2015 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Jaguars vs. Colts - Box Score - October 4, 2015 - ESPN|url = https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=400791671|website = ESPN.com|access-date = January 2, 2016}}</ref> On January 1, 2016, Jones was placed on injured reserve.<ref name="c928">{{Cite web |date=2016-01-01 |title=Jaguars place Abry Jones on IR, sign Richard Ash from PS |url=https://www.firstcoastnews.com/article/sports/jaguars-place-abry-jones-on-ir-sign-richard-ash-from-ps/77-17721957 |access-date=2025-03-15 |website=First Coast News}}</ref>

On February 15, 2017, Jones signed a four-year, $16 million contract extension with the Jaguars.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars sign DT Abry Jones to four-year, $16M deal|url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000785895/article/jaguars-sign-dt-abry-jones-to-fouryear-16m-deal|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170216054821/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000785895/article/jaguars-sign-dt-abry-jones-to-fouryear-16m-deal|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 16, 2017|author=Bergman, Jeremy|website=NFL.com|date=February 14, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=February 15, 2017 |title=Jaguars re-sign Abry Jones |url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-re-sign-Abry-Jones/f8c24369-8b5a-4ec5-acd8-e384412149ad |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> On September 10, 2017, in the season opener against the [[2017 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]], Jones's teammate [[Yannick Ngakoue]] forced a fumble off of quarterback [[Tom Savage (American football)|Tom Savage]]. The fumble was recovered by Jones and set the Jaguars' offense up for a touchdown scoring drive.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100htx.htm|title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Houston Texans - September 10th, 2017|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=October 6, 2017}}</ref>

On October 22, 2020, Jones was placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 22, 2020 |title=Jaguars Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-make-roster-moves-x3412 |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He was designated to return from injured reserve on November 25, and began practicing with the team again,<ref>{{cite news |title=Jaguars' Abry Jones: Receives return designation |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/jaguars-abry-jones-receives-return-designation/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=November 25, 2020 |access-date=February 2, 2021}}</ref> but the team did not activate him before his practice period expired on December 16.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jaguars' Abry Jones: Shut down for season |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/jaguars-abry-jones-shut-down-for-season/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=December 16, 2020 |access-date=February 2, 2021}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On June 3, 2021, Jones signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Add Veteran D-Linemen Trevon Coley and Abry Jones While Waiving Two Others|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-add-veteran-d-linemen-trevon-coley-and-abry-jones-while-parting-ways-with|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=June 3, 2021}}</ref> He announced his retirement from the NFL on July 24.<ref name="q221">{{cite web | last=Shipley | first=John | title=Former Jaguars NT Abry Jones Retires | website=SI.com| date=2021-07-24 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/jaguars/news/former-jaguars-nt-abry-jones-retires | access-date=2024-12-17}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jones' cousin [[Javontae Jean-Baptiste]] was selected by the [[Washington Commanders]] in the 7th round of the [[2024 NFL draft]].<ref name="h924">{{cite web | last=Lind | first=Andrew | title=What Javontae Jean-Baptiste's Commitment Means For Ohio State's 2018 Recruiting Class | website=Eleven Warriors | date=2018-02-07 | url=https://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-football-recruiting/2018/01/90435/what-javontae-jean-baptistes-commitment-means-for-ohio-states-2018-recruiting-class?amp | access-date=2024-12-17}}</ref>

'''Adam Replogle''' (born October 10, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player for the [[Atlanta Falcons]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] as a [[defensive tackle]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana Hoosiers]]. He converted to an [[offensive guard]] as a professional player.

==Indiana==
Replogle attended [[Indiana University Bloomington]] and played football as a defensive tackle for the [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Hoosiers]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Replogle IU's man in the middle: Defensive tackle sets the example for Hoosier defense|newspaper=[[The Herald-Times]]|date=November 6, 2012|url=https://www.hoosiertimes.com/herald_times_online/sports/college/iu/replogle-iu-s-man-in-the-middle/article_747ff5d3-5fb8-5887-8951-851faa0ef2b2.html}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>  He started 47 consecutive games for the Hoosiers from 2009 to 2012, missing the start only in the first game of his freshman season.<ref>{{cite news|title=NFL Draft name to know: Adam Replogle, DT from Indiana|work=CBS Sports|date=April 16, 2013|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/nfl-draft-name-to-know-adam-replogle-dt-from-indiana/#googDisableSync}}</ref> His 47 starts is an Indiana school record. He closed his collegiate career with 184 tackles, 15 sacks, 28.5 tackles for loss (110), three forced fumbles and one fumble recovery.<ref name=Bio>{{cite web|title=Adam Reploge|publisher=Indiana University|access-date=January 28, 2019|url=https://iuhoosiers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3957}}</ref> As a senior in 2012, he was selected both as a team captain and as the team's most valuable player.<ref name=Bio/> He was also named a first-team Academic All-American at the end of the 2012 season.<ref>{{cite news|newspaper=Indianapolis Examiner|date=December 6, 2012|title=IU's Replogle named first-team Academic All-America}}</ref>  In 2017, the [[Indianapolis Star]] named him one of the 25 best football players of the previous 25 years for Indiana University.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2017/08/28/best-iu-football-players-past-25-years/606159001/|title=Best 25 IU Football Players of All Time|access-date=January 29, 2019|date=August 28, 2017|first=Matthew|last=Glesesk}}</ref>

==Professional football==
Repologle was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in April 2013.<ref>{{cite news|newspaper=Herald-Times (Bloomington, IN)|date=April 28, 2013 |title=Black, Replogle ink free-agent deals}}</ref> He was cut by the Falcons during training camp but eventually signed on as a member of the practice squad in September 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.thefalcoholic.com/2014/9/30/6874607/falcons-sign-adam-replogle-kimario-mcfadden-to-practice-squad|title=Falcons Sign Adam Replogle, Kimario McFadden to Practice Squad|date=September 30, 2014}}</ref> Replogle was with the Falcons again in the 2015 off-season but did not make the final cut as the Falcons waived-injured him on September 5, 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/blog/article-1/Falcons-Reach-52-Man-Roster/7597ea7c-5788-4280-9657-a3b7aade9941 |title=Falcons Reach 52-Man Roster |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=September 5, 2015 |website=AtlantaFalcons.com |access-date=September 12, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150914221123/http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/blog/article-1/Falcons-Reach-52-Man-Roster/7597ea7c-5788-4280-9657-a3b7aade9941 |archive-date=September 14, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Adam Humphries''' (born June 24, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]] and signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in 2015. Humphries was also a member of the [[Tennessee Titans]], [[Washington Football Team]], and [[Houston Texans]].

==Early life==
Humphries was born in [[Spartanburg, South Carolina|Spartanburg]], [[South Carolina]] on June 24, 1993. He attended [[Dorman High School]] in [[Roebuck, South Carolina]] and played [[Varsity team#North America|varsity]] [[high school football|football]] and [[basketball]] for the Cavaliers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boynton |first=Eric |date=August 27, 2018 |title=Former Dorman, Clemson receiver Adam Humphries has viral moment |url=https://www.goupstate.com/news/20180827/former-dorman-clemson-receiver-adam-humphries-has-viral-moment |access-date=December 15, 2018 |website=GoUpstate |language=en |archive-date=April 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401175721/https://www.goupstate.com/news/20180827/former-dorman-clemson-receiver-adam-humphries-has-viral-moment |url-status=live }}</ref>

==College career==
Humphries played 53 games and started 27 of them for [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]] from 2011 to 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Humphries College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adam-humphries-1.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801192923/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adam-humphries-1.html |archive-date=August 1, 2019 |access-date=December 15, 2018 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Through his college career, Humphries had a total of 127 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 1,097 yards (8.6 avg.) and three [[touchdowns]], as well as 10 [[Carry (gridiron football)|carries]] for 24 yards and a touchdown and 69 [[punt return]]s for 476 yards (6.9 avg.) and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Adam Humphries |url=http://www.buccaneers.com/team-and-stats/roster/Adam-Humphries/25782a0d-ada3-4132-956a-4f70a4fbd90b |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180522022353/http://www.buccaneers.com/team-and-stats/roster/Adam-Humphries/25782a0d-ada3-4132-956a-4f70a4fbd90b |archive-date=May 22, 2018 |access-date=April 30, 2016 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref>

====2016 season====
Humphries entered training camp competing with Russell Shepard and [[Kenny Bell]] to be the Buccaneers' third wide receiver. New head coach [[Dirk Koetter]] named Humphries the team's third receiver.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=August 1, 2016 |title=Adam Humphries Slots in as the Third Receiver |url=http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Adam-Humphries-Slots-in-as-the-Third-Receiver/ad85a9d0-0749-4cc1-9c97-39ef7be0fb39 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160803004149/http://www.buccaneers.com/news/article-smith/Adam-Humphries-Slots-in-as-the-Third-Receiver/ad85a9d0-0749-4cc1-9c97-39ef7be0fb39 |archive-date=August 3, 2016 |access-date=August 2, 2016 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref>

Humphries earned his first NFL start in the season opener against the [[Atlanta Falcons]] and finished the 31–24 road victory with three receptions for 34 yards and a seven-yard carry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Atlanta Falcons – September 11th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110atl.htm |access-date=December 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=July 30, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170730095634/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110atl.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Two weeks later against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Humphries had his first 100-yard game, catching a season-high nine passes for 100 yards in the 37–32 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Jeff |date=September 26, 2016 |title=Rams vs. Buccaneers: 4 takeaways from the Rams 37–32 win |url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2016/09/25/rams-vs-buccaneers-4-takeaways-from-the-rams-37-32-win/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181216032156/https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2016/09/25/rams-vs-buccaneers-4-takeaways-from-the-rams-37-32-win/ |archive-date=December 16, 2018 |access-date=December 15, 2018 |website=The Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en}}</ref>

During Week 9 against the Falcons, Humphries recorded five receptions for 46 yards and his first touchdown of the season on a seven-yard pass from Jameis Winston in the 43–28 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers – November 3rd, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611030tam.htm |access-date=December 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=August 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170814023318/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611030tam.htm |url-status=live}}</ref> During a Week 15 26–20 road loss to the [[Dallas Cowboys]], Humphries caught two passes for 49 yards and a season-long 42-yard touchdown reception.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys – December 18th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612180dal.htm |access-date=November 18, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 17, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180117071810/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612180dal.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> In the regular season finale against the [[Carolina Panthers]], Humphries had a career-high 10 receptions for 94 yards during the narrow 17–16 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hope |first=Dan |date=January 2, 2017 |title=Tigers in the NFL: Humphries has first 10-catch game |url=https://www.independentmail.com/story/sports/college/clemson/football/2017/01/02/tigers-nfl-adam-humphries-deandre-hopkins-dwayne-allen-vic-beasley/96065770/ |access-date=December 15, 2018 |website=Independent Mail |language=en |archive-date=October 22, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022205242/https://www.independentmail.com/story/sports/college/clemson/football/2017/01/02/tigers-nfl-adam-humphries-deandre-hopkins-dwayne-allen-vic-beasley/96065770/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Humphries finished his second professional season with 55 receptions for 622 yards and three touchdowns in 15 games and four starts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sauers |first=Zach |date=July 13, 2017 |title=Buccaneers: The emergence of Adam Humphries |url=https://thepewterplank.com/2017/07/13/buccaneers-emergence-adam-humphries/ |access-date=December 15, 2018 |website=The Pewter Plank |language=en-US |archive-date=December 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181216031557/https://thepewterplank.com/2017/07/13/buccaneers-emergence-adam-humphries/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2017 season====
On February 27, 2017, Humphries signed a one-year guaranteed contract tender with the Buccaneers worth $615,000.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Auman |first=Greg |date=February 27, 2017 |title=Bucs tender WR Adam Humphries, 3 others for 2017 |url=http://www.tampabay.com/blogs/bucs/bucs-tender-wr-adam-humphries-3-others-for-2017/2314729 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307072626/http://www.tampabay.com/blogs/bucs/bucs-tender-wr-adam-humphries-3-others-for-2017/2314729 |archive-date=March 7, 2017 |access-date=February 28, 2017 |website=TampaBay.com}}</ref> He entered the season third on the wide receiver depth chart behind [[Mike Evans (wide receiver)|Mike Evans]] and [[DeSean Jackson]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers Depth Chart Archive |url=https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/199/TB |access-date=December 15, 2018 |website=www.ourlads.com |archive-date=December 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181216031130/https://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/199/TB |url-status=live }}</ref>

During a Week 15 24–21 loss to the Falcons on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'', Humphries had five receptions for 43 yards and his only touchdown of the season to go along with a six-yard carry.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - December 18th, 2017|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712180tam.htm|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=2026-01-29|language=en}}</ref> In the regular season finale against the Saints, Humphries recorded seven receptions for 102 yards in the 31–24 victory.<ref>{{Cite web|title=New Orleans Saints at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - December 31st, 2017|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712310tam.htm|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=2026-01-29|language=en}}</ref>

Humphries finished the 2017 season with a career-high 61 receptions for 631 yards and a touchdown in 16 games and three starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Humphries 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HumpAd00.htm |access-date=December 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=December 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181216071152/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HumpAd00.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2018 season====
On March 12, 2018, the Buccaneers placed a second-round restricted free agent tender on Humphries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=March 12, 2018 |title=Bucs tender Adam Humphries, re-sign Adarius Glanton |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/03/12/bucs-tender-adam-humphries-re-sign-adarius-glanton/ |access-date=June 4, 2020 |website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com |archive-date=April 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401180932/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/03/12/bucs-tender-adam-humphries-re-sign-adarius-glanton/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

During a Week 11 38–35 road loss to the [[New York Giants]], Humphries caught three passes for 60 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Highlights: Winston Touchdown to Humphries |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/video/highlights-winston-touchdown-to-humphries-19124165?campaign=sf:fanshare:facebook |access-date=December 15, 2018 |website=www.buccaneers.com |language=en-US}}</ref> In the next game against the [[San Francisco 49ers]], he recorded six receptions for 50 yards and a touchdown during the 27–9 victory.<ref name="Easterling">{{Cite web |last=Easterling |first=Luke |date=November 25, 2018 |title=Bucs stretch lead over 49ers with Jameis Winston, Adam Humphries TD |url=https://bucswire.usatoday.com/2018/11/25/watch-bucs-stretch-lead-over-49ers-with-jameis-winston-adam-humphries-td/ |access-date=December 15, 2018 |website=Bucs Wire |language=en}}</ref> The following week against the Panthers, Humphries had seven receptions for 61 yards and a touchdown in the 24–17 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Arcia |first=Gil |date=December 3, 2018 |title=Notes and highlights from the Buccaneers 24-17 win over the Panthers |url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2018/12/3/18122870/notes-highlights-from-the-buccaneers-24-17-win-over-the-panthers |access-date=December 15, 2018 |website=Bucs Nation}}</ref> During Week 15 against the Cowboys, he caught 10 passes for 79 yards in the 27–20 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Dallas Cowboys - December 23rd, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812230dal.htm |access-date=April 1, 2019 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Humphries finished the 2018 season with career highs in receptions with 76, receiving yards with 816, and touchdowns with five in 16 games and 10 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Humphries 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HumpAd00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=April 1, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401175309/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HumpAd00/gamelog/2018/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
====2019 season====
[[File:Adam Humphries 2019 10-13.jpg|thumb|Humphries in 2019]]
On March 14, 2019, Humphries signed a four-year, $36 million contract with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=March 14, 2019 |title=Titans Agree to Terms with Former Buccaneers WR Adam Humphries |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-agree-to-terms-with-former-buccaneers-wr-adam-humphries |access-date=June 4, 2020 |website=TitansOnline.com |archive-date=April 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401183700/https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-agree-to-terms-with-former-buccaneers-wr-adam-humphries |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Teope |first=Herbie |date=March 11, 2019 |title=Titans sign Adam Humphries to 4-year contract |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/titans-sign-adam-humphries-to-4-year-contract-0ap3000001022019 |access-date=June 4, 2020 |website=National Football League |archive-date=April 28, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428162244/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001022019/article/titans-to-sign-adam-humphries-to-4year-contract |url-status=live }}</ref>

During a Week 10 35–32 victory over the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], Humphries caught his first touchdown of the season on a 23-yard reception from [[Ryan Tannehill]], which proved to be the game-winner.<ref name="Brian">{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Tennessee Titans – November 10th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201911100oti.htm |access-date=June 4, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=June 11, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611134240/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201911100oti.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Three weeks later against the [[Indianapolis Colts]], Humphries caught his second touchdown of the season on a 13-yard reception in the 31–17 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts – December 1st, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201912010clt.htm |access-date=June 4, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=June 11, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611134407/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201912010clt.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Humphries did not play in the last four games of the regular season due to an ankle injury.

Humphries finished the 2019 season with 37 receptions for 374 yards and two touchdowns in 12 games and three starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Humphries 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HumpAd00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=June 4, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221118201824/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HumpAd00/gamelog/2019/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He returned from injury in the [[2019–20 NFL playoffs#AFC: Kansas City Chiefs 35, Tennessee Titans 24|AFC Championship Game]] against the Chiefs and finished the 35–24 road loss with four receptions for 25 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AFC Championship - Tennessee Titans at Kansas City Chiefs - January 19th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202001190kan.htm |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2020 season====
During Week 2 against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], Humphries caught six passes for 48 yards and his first touchdown of the season in the 33–30 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Tennessee Titans - September 20th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009200oti.htm |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On October 2, 2020, Humphries was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Benjamin |first=Cody |last2=Sullivan |first2=Tyler |date=October 2, 2020 |title=Two more Titans, including Adam Humphries test positive for COVID-19, Week 5 reportedly also in jeopardy |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/two-more-titans-including-adam-humphries-test-positive-for-covid-19-week-5-reportedly-also-in-jeopardy/ |access-date=October 9, 2020 |website=CBS Sports |archive-date=October 9, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201009013102/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/two-more-titans-including-adam-humphries-test-positive-for-covid-19-week-5-reportedly-also-in-jeopardy/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was activated on October 14.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 14, 2020 |title=Titans' Adam Humphries: Lifted from reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/titans-adam-humphries-lifted-from-reservecovid-19-list/ |access-date=October 30, 2020 |website=CBSSports.com |archive-date=January 15, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115175543/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/titans-adam-humphries-lifted-from-reservecovid-19-list/ |url-status=live }}</ref> During a Week 6 42–36 overtime victory over the [[Houston Texans]], Humphries had six receptions for a season-high 64 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Tennessee Titans - October 18th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010180oti.htm |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Two weeks later against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], he left the eventual 31–20 road loss at halftime due to a concussion and missed the next four games as a result.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davenport |first=Turron |date=2020-11-01 |title=Tennessee Titans WR Adam Humphries out for game with concussion |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/30238514/tennessee-titans-wr-adam-humphries-game-concussion |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

On December 8, 2020, Humphries was placed on [[injured reserve]] due to the lingering concussion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=December 8, 2020 |title=Titans Place WR Adam Humphries on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-place-wr-adam-humphries-on-injured-reserve |access-date=November 18, 2022 |website=Tennessee Titans |archive-date=January 24, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220124024859/https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-place-wr-adam-humphries-on-injured-reserve |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished the 2020 season with 23 receptions for 228 yards and two touchdowns in seven games and one start.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Humphries 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HumpAd00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=November 18, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221118201823/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HumpAd00/gamelog/2020/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Without Humphries, the Titans finished atop the AFC South with an 11–5 record and lost to the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the [[2020–21 NFL playoffs#AFC: Baltimore Ravens 20, Tennessee Titans 13|Wild Card Round]] by a score of 20–13.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2020 Tennessee Titans Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/oti/2020.htm|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=2026-01-29|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Wild Card - Baltimore Ravens at Tennessee Titans - January 10th, 2021|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101100oti.htm|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=2026-01-29|language=en}}</ref>

Humphries was released by the Titans on February 25, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=February 25, 2021 |title=Titans Release WR Adam Humphries, Part Ways With DBs Chris Milton and Breon Borders, While Adding Former 49ers DL Jullian Taylor |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-release-wr-adam-humphries-part-ways-with-dbs-chris-milton-and-breon-borde |access-date=November 18, 2022 |website=Tennessee Titans |archive-date=January 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128201259/https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-release-wr-adam-humphries-part-ways-with-dbs-chris-milton-and-breon-borde |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''Adam Gotsis''' (born 23 September 1992) is an Australian professional [[American football]] [[defensive end]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets football|Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets]] and was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the second round of the [[2016 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] and [[Indianapolis Colts]].

==Early life==
Gotsis was born in [[Melbourne]], Australia, to parents of [[Greeks|Greek]] heritage, he was raised in the suburb of [[Abbotsford, Victoria|Abbotsford]]. He grew up playing [[Australian rules football]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/us-sports/australians-adam-gotsis-tom-hackett-hopeful-ahead-of-nfl-draft-20160427-gogrpa.html|title=Australians Adam Gotsis, Tom Hackett hopeful ahead of NFL draft|date=28 April 2016|publisher=|via=The Sydney Morning Herald}}</ref> and supported the [[North Melbourne Football Club]] in the [[Australian Football League]]. At the age of 13, while attending [[Kew High School]], his interest in Australian rules football had waned and his mother discovered a local junior [[American football]] club via a [[Google]] search, the [[Monash Warriors]], that Gotsis and his older brother would later join.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wl8EaI9D8Fw|title=Georgia Tech Football: Adam Gotsis|last=Georgia Tech Athletics|date=27 September 2012|publisher=|via=YouTube}}</ref> He recorded a team-high 12.5 sacks and earned league MVP honors in 2010. He progressed through the local ranks and eventually represented the [[Australia national American football team|Australian national American football team]] at the [[2011 IFAF World Championship|IFAF World Championship]] in December 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gridironaustralia.org.au/2011/ifaf-announces-first-of-12-players-named-to-world-team-roster-to-face-usa-in-annual-international-bowl/|title=IFAF announces first of 12 players named to World Team roster to face USA in annual International Bowl - Gridiron Australia|website=gridironaustralia.org.au}}</ref> A month later, Gotsis signed to play [[college football]] for [[Georgia Institute of Technology|Georgia Tech]] and arrived in [[Atlanta]] in July 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gridironaustralia.org.au/2012/australian-dt-adam-gotsis-commits-to-georgia-tech/|title=Australian DT Adam Gotsis commits to Georgia Tech - Gridiron Australia|website=gridironaustralia.org.au}}</ref>

==College career==
Gotsis spent four years playing college football for the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets football]] team. Gotsis appeared in 48 games (37 starts) at Georgia Tech, totaling 110 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]] (69 solo), 12.5 [[qb sack|sacks]], two [[interception]]s, two [[fumble]] recoveries and four blocked kicks. He started the first nine games of his senior season, finishing the year with 31 tackles (20 solo), five tackles for loss, a team-best three sacks and two fumble recoveries before a season-ending knee injury. Gotsis started all 14 games along the defensive line his junior season, posting 36 tackles (23 solo), three sacks, one interception, three passes defensed and two blocked kicks. He was named to the All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] Second-team by both the media and coaches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://files.denverbroncos.com/resources/custom/Images/email_blast/2018_Denver_Broncos_Media_Guide_a.pdf|title=2018 Denver Broncos Media Guide|access-date=2023-02-02|archive-date=16 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191216001512/http://files.denverbroncos.com/resources/custom/Images/email_blast/2018_Denver_Broncos_Media_Guide_a.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> Gotsis started all 13 games of his sophomore season at [[nose tackle]], recording 38 tackles (23 solo), 5.5 sacks, one interception and one pass defensed in addition to blocking two kicks. He ranked second on team in tackles for loss (14.5) and sacks (5.5). He graduated from Georgia Tech with a degree in [[Business Administration]] in December 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.myajc.com/news/sports/college/how-adam-gotsis-made-himself-an-nfl-draft-prospect/nrDWf/|title=How Adam Gotsis made himself an NFL draft prospect|date=28 April 2016|author=Ken Sugiura|work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bcsnn.com/acc/8774-denver-broncos-take-gotsis-despite-knee-issues.html|title=Denver Broncos Take Gotsis Despite Knee Issues|publisher=|access-date=1 May 2016|archive-date=9 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181109213406/http://www.bcsnn.com/acc/8774-denver-broncos-take-gotsis-despite-knee-issues.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
Gotsis was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the second round (63rd overall) in the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/2016/04/30/nfl-broncos-welcome-aussie-pick-gotsis|title=NFL Broncos welcome Aussie pick Gotsis|date=30 April 2016 |publisher=}}</ref> He became the highest-drafted Australian-born player in [[NFL]] history. On 26 May 2016, the Broncos announced that they had signed Gotsis to a four-year, $5.40 million contract with a signing bonus of $1.06 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/us-sports/nfl-adam-gotsis-officially-signs-rookie-contract-with-denver-broncos-for-a54-million/news-story/4681cee2d76ea9fa7a41bacabc7abe50?nk=af35f5cc355f5a711a84fd71bbe82676-1737456695|title=NFL: Adam Gotsis officially signs rookie contract with Denver Broncos for $5.4 million|access-date=14 November 2016|author=Melanie Dinjaski|date=27 May 2016|website=foxsports.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161115131932/https://amp.foxsports.com.au/nfl/nfl-adam-gotsis-officially-signs-rookie-contract-with-denver-broncos-for-a54-million/news-story/4681cee2d76ea9fa7a41bacabc7abe50|archive-date=15 November 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Gotsis played all 16 games and finished with 14 tackles (5 solo), one pass defensed and one fumble recovery. Gotsis made his NFL debut vs. the [[Carolina Panthers]] on 8 September 2016.

In 2017, Gotsis started 13-of-16 games played, totaling 41 tackles (28 solo), two sacks, four passes defensed and one fumble recovery. He earned his first NFL start and made four tackles (2 solo) vs. the [[Dallas Cowboys]] on 17 September 2017. Gotsis recorded his first career sack and blocked a field goal vs. the [[New York Giants]] on 15 October 2017.

On 23 December 2019, Gotsis was placed on [[injured reserve]] after undergoing knee surgery.

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On 2 August 2020, Gotsis signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars sign veteran defensive end Adam Gotsis|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/08/02/jaguars-sign-veteran-defensive-end-adam-gotsis/|author=Gantt, Darin|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=August 2, 2020}}</ref>

Gotsis re-signed with the Jaguars on 25 March 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jaguars Re-Sign Defensive End Adam Gotsis |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-sign-defensive-end-adam-gotsis |website=Jaguars.com |date=March 25, 2021 |access-date=March 25, 2021}}</ref> He played in 16 games with four starts, recording three sacks and 27 tackles.

On 4 May 2022, Gotsis re-signed with the Jaguars.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Jaguars re-sign DL Adam Gotsis|url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jaguars-re-sign-dl-adam-gotsis|website=Jaguars.com|date=May 4, 2022}}</ref>

On 20 March 2023, Gotsis again re–signed with Jacksonville.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 20, 2023 |title=Roster Moves: Jaguars Re-Sign Defensive Lineman Adam Gotsis |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jaguars-re-sign-defensive-lineman-adam-gotsis |access-date=April 29, 2024 |website=Jaguars.com |language=en}}</ref> He appeared in all 17 games for Jacksonville in 2023, logging 26 combined tackles, 4 pass deflections, and 1 sack.

Gotsis was waived by the Jaguars on August 6, 2024.<ref name="l339">{{cite web | last=Harvey | first=Demetrius | title=Jacksonville Jaguars sign S Adrian Amos, DT Jonathan Marshall | website=Florida Times-Union | date=2024-08-06 | url=https://www.jacksonville.com/story/sports/nfl/jaguars/2024/08/06/jacksonville-jaguars-sign-adrian-amos-jonathan-marshall-wingard-injury/74693295007/ | access-date=2024-12-18}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On September 17, 2024, Gotsis signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Colts place DT DeForest Buckner on injured reserve; sign DE Genard Avery to 53-man roster from practice squad; make additional practice squad roster moves |url=https://www.colts.com/news/deforest-buckner-injured-reserve-defensive-tackle-genard-avery-adam-gotsis-practice-squad |website=colts.com |access-date=18 September 2024}}</ref> Later in the 2024 season, Gotsis was elevated for a Week 4 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. He was released on November 16.<ref name="k510">{{cite web | title=Colts sign LB Liam Anderson to 53-man roster from practice squad; elevate G Atonio Mafi, G Josh Sills to active roster from practice squad for Week 11; release DT Adam Gotsis | website=Colts.com | date=2024-11-16 | url=https://www.colts.com/news/liam-anderson-signed-53-man-roster-linebacker-josh-sills-atonio-mafi-adam-gotsis-roster-moves | access-date=2024-12-18}}</ref>

=== Tampa Bay Buccaneers ===
On January 8, 2025, Gotsis was signed to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=2025-01-08 |title=Troy Hill Designated for Return, Adam Gotsis Signed to Practice Squad |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/troy-hill-designated-return-adam-gotsis-signed-practice-squad |access-date=2025-01-09 |website=Buccaneers.com |language=}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract on January 21.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Ink DL Adam Gotsis, P Jake Julien to Futures Deals|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-ink-dl-adam-gotsis-p-jake-julien-futures-deals|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=January 21, 2025}}</ref> He was released on August 26 as part of final roster cuts and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Scott |title=Bucs Load Up in the Trenches on First Practice Squad of 2025 |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-load-trenches-first-practice-squad-2025 |website=buccaneers.com |access-date=1 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Scott |title=Kyle Trask, Trey Palmer Among Cuts as Bucs Get Roster Down to 53 |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/kyle-trask-trey-palmer-among-cuts-bucs-get-roster-down-53 |website=buccaneers.com |access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref> During Week 1, Gotsis was elevated to the active roster.

== Controversy ==
In March 2018, Gotsis was arrested for alleged rape of a woman in 2013,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2018/mar/13/denver-broncos-adam-gotsis-arrested-over-alleged-2013|title=Denver Broncos' Adam Gotsis arrested over alleged 2013 rape|last=Agencies|date=13 March 2018|website=the Guardian|language=en|access-date=13 March 2018}}</ref> while he was a [[Student athlete|student-athlete]] at Georgia Tech. He surrendered himself to [[Atlanta Police Department|Atlanta Police]] on 7 March 2018, and was released after posting $US 50,000.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sbs.com.au/news/australian-nfl-star-adam-gotsis-denies-us-rape-allegation|title=Australian NFL star Adam Gotsis denies US rape allegation|work=SBS News|access-date=13 March 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref> On 15 August 2018, the Fulton County District Attorney’s Office announced that it would not pursue charges against Gotsis.<ref name="h054">{{cite web | last=Legwold | first=Jeff | title=DA drops rape case against Broncos DE Gotsis | website=ESPN.com | date=2018-08-15 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/24384676/rape-case-denver-broncos-de-adam-gotsis-dropped | access-date=2024-10-02}}</ref>

'''Aaron Jon Wallace Jr.''' (born July 8, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[high school football]] at [[Rancho Bernardo High School]] and [[college football]] for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]].<ref>[http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=207914058 "Bio for Aaron Wallace"]. uclabruins.com. Retrieved May 13, 2016.</ref> His father [[Aaron Wallace]] also played in the NFL.

==Professional career==

'''Adairius Damone Barnes''' (born April 30, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech Bulldogs]].

==Early life==
Barnes attended [[Port Gibson High School]] where he [[Varsity letter|lettered]] in [[high school football|football]], [[track & field]], [[baseball]], and [[high school basketball|basketball]]. As a [[Eleventh grade|junior]] in 2010, he rushed the ball 17 times for 214 yards and five [[touchdowns]], while recording 27 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 647 yards and three touchdowns. As a [[Twelfth grade|senior]] in 2011, he rushed the ball 24 times for 390 yards and four touchdowns. he also was 15-of-28 for 428 yards and three touchdowns. He also recorded 22 receptions for 512 yards and six touchdowns. Also that season he recorded 45 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]], 11 pass deflections, one [[interception]], one forced [[fumble]], four [[punt returns]] for 47 yards and two [[kickoff return]]s for 25 yards. For the season, he was ranked 24th on the Top 50 players in [[Mississippi]]. He was also named the team's best offensive player.<ref name="La. Tech bio">{{cite web |url=http://www.latechsports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/adairius_barnes_793204.html |title=Adairius Barnes bio |website=LaTechSports.com |access-date=October 4, 2016 |archive-date=October 5, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005120232/http://www.latechsports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/adairius_barnes_793204.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
Barnes then attended [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech]]. As freshman in [[2012 Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football team|2012]], he recorded five tackles (three solo), he also recorded one reception on a [[fake punt]] from [[Ryan Allen (American football)|Ryan Allen]]. As a sophomore in [[2013 Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football team|2013]], he appeared in all 12 games with 11 stars. he recorded 49 tackles (31 solo), one [[Quarterback sack|sack]], a team leading four interceptions, one forced fumble and seven [[passes defensed]]. For the season, he was named All-[[Conference USA]] honorable mention. In [[2014 Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football team|2014]] as a junior, he recorded 46 tackles (30 solo), four [[tackles-for-loss]], nine passes defensed, and five interceptions. As a senior in [[2015 Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football team|2015]], he recorded 50 tackles (39 solo), 1.5 tackles-for-loss, one interception, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. For the season, he was named All-Conference USA honorable mention and second-team All-Louisiana.<ref name="La. Tech bio" />
