'''Adam Shaheen''' (born October 24, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ashland Eagles football|Ashland Eagles]], and was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the second round of the [[2017 NFL draft]]. He is the highest draft pick from Ashland in the modern era of the NFL.{{Cn|date=November 2025}}

==Early life==
Shaheen attended [[Big Walnut High School]] in [[Sunbury, Ohio]]. He played [[high school football|football]] and [[basketball]] in high school.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Shaheen's High School Timeline |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/adam-shaheen/RrMuDvTsEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/default.htm |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=MaxPreps.com |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
Shaheen played one year of [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Pittsburgh at Johnstown]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rabinowitz |first=Bill |date=March 2, 2017 |title=Big Walnut graduate transforms into NFL-ready tight end |url=http://www.dispatch.com/sports/20170302/nfl-combine--big-walnut-graduate-transforms-into-nfl-ready-tight-end |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=The Columbus Dispatch}}</ref> In 2014, he transferred to [[Ashland University]] and joined the football team as a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pluto |first=Terry |author-link=Terry Pluto |date=March 1, 2017 |title=Ashland's Adam Shaheen: Amazing story of biggest surprise at NFL Combine |url=https://www.cleveland.com/pluto/2017/03/ashlands_adam_shaheen_the_amaz.html |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=The Plain Dealer |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rabinowitz |first=Amanda |title=The View From Pluto: An Ashland Walk-On Who's Now the NFL's Most Unlikely Prospect |url=https://www.wksu.org/post/view-pluto-ashland-walk-whos-now-nfls-most-unlikely-prospect |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=WKSU |date=March 2017 |language=en}}</ref> During his career, he had 129 [[football catch|receptions]] for 1,755 yards and 26 [[touchdowns]]. After the 2016 season, Shaheen decided to forgo his senior year and enter the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 5, 2017 |title=Door's open: Ashland U tight end turning pro |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/football/2017/01/05/ashland-eagles-shaheen/96204372/ |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=USA TODAY |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Conrad |first=Curt |date=January 5, 2017 |title=AU's Shaheen going pro |url=https://www.richlandsource.com/2017/01/05/aus-shaheen-going-pro/ |access-date=2025-02-23 |website=Richland Source}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
On January 5, 2017, it was announced that Shaheen would forgo his senior season and enter the [[2017 NFL draft]]. At the time of the announcement, he was ranked the 12th best [[tight end]] prospect in the draft by [[CBS Sports]] and NFLDraftScout.com.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kesselring |first=Colt |date=January 5, 2017 |title=D2 Football Tight End Adam Shaheen Declares Early For NFL Draft |url=https://www.herosports.com/amp/news/d2-football-tight-end-adam-shaheen-declares-early-nfl-draft |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=HeroSports.com}}{{Dead link|date=June 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Shaheen was one of 19 tight ends invited to the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]]. He fared well in the combine drills and tied [[2016 Oregon Ducks football|Oregon's]] [[Pharaoh Brown]] for first in the bench press with 24 reps.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lyles Jr. |first=Harry |date=March 5, 2016 |title=NFL Combine results 2017: Full tight end numbers |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2017/3/3/14802746/2017-nfl-combine-results-o-j-howard-evan-engram-jake-butt |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=SBNation.com}}</ref> Shaheen had his best performance during positional drills, showing his agility and receiving ability. He received a boost in his draft stock after he impressed scouts and team representatives with his performance in the positional drills.

Prior to the combine, Shaheen was a relatively unknown prospect out of [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] [[Ashland University]]. He received media attention after an interview at the combine where he was asked by a reporter how he gained 70 lbs. during college, with Shaheen responding, "Um, a lot of [[Chipotle]] burritos." He went on to reiterate, "In all honesty, it was a lot of burritos." The quote and story went on to be posted on websites by the [[Bleacher Report]], [[New York Daily News]], ''[[USA Today]]'', and [[ESPN]], with the [[New England Patriots|New England Patriots']] website donning him the "Chipotle Prospect".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Parco |first=Nicholas |date=March 4, 2017 |title=NFL prospect Adam Shaheen bulked up by eating 'a lot of Chipotle |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/football/nfl-prospect-adam-shaheen-bulked-eating-lot-chipotle-article-1.2988400 |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=New York Daily News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gagnon |first=Brad |date=April 20, 2017 |title=Adam Shaheen: The NFL Draft's Most Mysterious Man |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2702010-adam-shaheen-the-nfl-drafts-most-mysterious-man |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=BleacherReport.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dickerson |first=Jeff |date=May 18, 2017 |title=Massive TE Adam Shaheen gets Chipotle fix at rookie camp |url=http://www.espn.com/blog/chicago-bears/post/_/id/4705577/bears-second-rounder-adam-shaheen-gets-chipotle-fix-at-rookie-camp |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tsuji |first=Alysha |date=March 3, 2017 |title=NFL draft prospect says 'a lot of Chipotle burritos' helped him gain weight |url=https://www.ftw.usatoday.com/2017/03/nfl-draft-prospect-adam-shaheen-chipotle-burritos-weight-gain/amp |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170504015152/http://ftw.usatoday.com/2017/03/nfl-draft-prospect-adam-shaheen-chipotle-burritos-weight-gain/amp |archive-date=May 4, 2017 |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=For The Win|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> On March 22, 2017, Shaheen opted to participate at Ashland's [[Pro Day]] and chose to only run positional drills. Scouts and team representatives from 16 NFL teams attended, including tight end coaches from the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], [[Chicago Bears]], [[New Orleans Saints]], [[Oakland Raiders]], and [[Detroit Lions]]. Shaheen had multiple visits and private workouts with NFL teams, including the [[Philadelphia Eagles]],  [[Cleveland Browns]], [[Tennessee Titans]], [[Arizona Cardinals]], [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], and [[Dallas Cowboys]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brandt |first=Gil |date=March 22, 2017 |title=Pro day results: USC, Miss. St., Michigan St., Pitt, UConn |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/pro-day-results-usc-miss-st-michigan-st-pitt-uconn-0ap3000000794596 |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Root |first=Jess |date=March 23, 2017 |title=Cardinals have private workout with TE Adam Shaheen |url=http://cardswire.usatoday.com/2017/03/23/cardinals-have-private-workout-with-te-adam-shaheen/ |access-date=May 28, 2017 |website=Cards Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> The majority of NFL draft experts and analysts projected him to be a second round pick. ===Chicago Bears===
====2017====
The [[Chicago Bears]] selected Shaheen in the second round with the 45th overall pick in the 2017 NFL draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer, Larry |date=April 28, 2017 |title=Bears pick TE Shaheen in Round 2 |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-pick-TE-Shaheen-in-Round-2/f9519bc1-9d05-478a-a306-79d78fb29c3f |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170430091137/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Bears-pick-TE-Shaheen-in-Round-2/f9519bc1-9d05-478a-a306-79d78fb29c3f |archive-date=April 30, 2017 |access-date=April 29, 2017 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref> The Bears originally owned the [[Budda Baker|36th overall]] pick in the second round, but opted to trade the selection with their seventh round pick [[Shalom Luani|(221st overall)]] to the Cardinals and acquired their second round (45th), fourth round [[Tarik Cohen|(119th overall)]], and sixth round picks [[Jeremy Clark (defensive back)|(197th overall)]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Perez |first=Bryan |date=May 3, 2017 |title=Todd McShay says Adam Shaheen is Bears' best pick from 2017 NFL Draft |url=https://bearswire.usatoday.com/2017/05/03/todd-mcshay-says-adam-shaheen-is-bears-best-pick-from-2017-nfl-draft/ |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=Bears Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref> Shaheen is the second-highest player to be drafted from [[Ashland University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ashland Players/Alumni |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/schools/ashland/ |access-date=2025-01-17 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He joins [[Jeris Pendleton]] ([[2012 NFL draft|2012]]), [[Bill Overmyer]] ([[1972 NFL draft|1972]]), and Len Pettigrew ([[1971 NFL draft|1971]]) as the only players to be drafted from Ashland.<ref>{{Cite web |title=247Sports: Ashland NFL Draft History |url=https://247sports.com/Team/Ashland-University-803/DraftPicks/?year=alltime |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=247sports.com}}</ref> On May 19, 2017, the Bears signed Shaheen to a four-year, $5.91 million contract with $3.17 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $2.43 million.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Adam Shaheen contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/chicago-bears/adam-shaheen-21786/ |access-date=May 28, 2017 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]], Shaheen competed against [[Daniel Brown (American football)|Daniel Brown]] and [[Ben Braunecker]] for the job as the third tight end on the depth chart.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Chicago Bears depth chart: 07/01/2017 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/depthchart/CHI |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=ourlads.com}}</ref> Head coach [[John Fox (American football)|John Fox]] named Shaheen the third tight end on the Bears' depth chart to begin the regular season, behind veterans [[Zach Miller (tight end, born 1984)|Zach Miller]] and [[Dion Sims]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears' depth chart |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/team/depth-chart.html |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Bears' season-opening 23–17 loss to the [[Atlanta Falcons]]. On September 24, Shaheen made his first career start and caught the first pass of his career on a two-yard touchdown pass from quarterback [[Mike Glennon]] during their 23–17 [[overtime (American football)|overtime]] victory. His first career  touchdown reception came in the second quarter as Shaheen was left wide open on a blown coverage by the Steelers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Chicago Bears – September 24th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709240chi.htm |access-date=November 5, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Throughout the first seven regular season games, Shaheen was predominantly used as a blocking tight end in two and three tight end sets. During a Week 8 matchup against the Saints, starting tight end Zach Miller suffered a dislocated knee and tore his [[popliteal artery]]. Miller was placed on [[injured reserve]] for the remainder of the season and Shaheen became the second starting tight end, along with Dion Sims.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Potash |first=Adam  |date=October 31, 2017 |title=With Zach Miller out, rookie Adam Shaheen has a chance to break out |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2017/10/31/18375546/with-zach-miller-out-rookie-adam-shaheen-has-a-chance-to-break-out/ |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=Chicago Sun-Times}}</ref> In Week 11, he made his third consecutive start and caught a season-high four passes for 41-yards and caught a one-yard touchdown pass from [[Mitchell Trubisky]] during the Bears' 27–24 loss to the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at Chicago Bears - November 19th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711190chi.htm |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On December 10, Shaheen caught four passes for a season-high 44 receiving yards and scored on a one-yard touchdown reception during Chicago's 33–7 routing of the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Cincinnati Bengals - December 10th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712100cin.htm |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He injured his chest during the game and was inactive for the following week.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Finley |first=Patrick |date=December 16, 2017 |title=Bears TE Adam Shaheen, S Adrian Amos out vs. Lions |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2017/12/16/18330344/bears-te-adam-shaheen-s-adrian-amos-out-vs-lions/ |access-date=December 19, 2017 |website=Chicago Sun-Times}}</ref> As a rookie, Shaheen finished with 12 receptions for 127 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Shaheen 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/ShahAd00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2018====
In 2018, Shaheen was slated to be the Bears starting tight end. However, in the team's second preseason game, Shaheen suffered a sprained ankle and foot. He was placed on injured reserve on September 2, 2018, with the possibility of returning later in the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer, Larry |date=September 2, 2018 |title=Roster Moves: Bears place Shaheen on IR, waive Grasu |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-place-shaheen-on-ir-waive-grasu |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=ChicagoBears.com |archive-date=September 23, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180923005657/https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-place-shaheen-on-ir-waive-grasu |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was activated off injured reserve on November 17, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 17, 2018 |title=Roster Moves: Bears activate Shaheen, Sims to IR |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-activate-shaheen-move-sims-to-ir |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref> Playing in six games, he recorded five catches for 48 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=February 7, 2019 |title=Bears 2018 position review: Tight end |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/bears-2018-position-review-tight-end |access-date=February 11, 2019 |publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]}}</ref>

====2019====
Shaheen entered the 2019 season second on the Bears tight end depth chart behind [[Trey Burton]]. He was placed on injured reserve on November 30, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=November 30, 2019 |title=Roster moves: Bears sign two; place two on IR |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-sign-two-place-two-on-ir |access-date=October 4, 2023 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref> He finished the season with nine catches for 74 yards and no touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Shaheen 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/ShahAd00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On July 26, 2020, Shaheen was traded to the [[Miami Dolphins]] for a conditional seventh-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=July 26, 2020 |title=Roster Moves: Bears trade Shaheen, release 3 |publisher=[[Chicago Bears]] |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-trade-shaheen-release-3 |access-date=July 26, 2020}}</ref> In Week 5 against the [[San Francisco 49ers]], he recorded his first touchdown with the Dolphins in the 43–17 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Miami Dolphins at San Francisco 49ers – October 11th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010110sfo.htm |access-date=October 18, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>
On October 28, 2020, Shaheen signed a two-year, $7.65 million contract extension with the Dolphins.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 28, 2020 |title=Tight End Adam Shaheen Signs Contract Extension |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/tight-end-adam-shaheen-signs-contract-extension |access-date=October 5, 2023 |website=MiamiDolphins.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished the 2020 season with 12 receptions for 150 receiving yards and three receiving touchdowns in 16 games and five starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Shaheen 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/ShahAd00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=October 5, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2021 season, Shaheen appeared in 12 games and started seven. He recorded 12 receptions for 110 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Shaheen 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/ShahAd00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=October 5, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On August 9, 2022, the Dolphins agreed to trade Shaheen along with a 2023 seventh-round pick to the [[Houston Texans]] in exchange for a 2023 sixth-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 9, 2022 |title=Roster Moves: Dolphins make trade with Houston |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/roster-moves-dolphins-make-trade-with-houston |access-date=October 4, 2023 |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref> Two days later, the trade was cancelled due to Shaheen being unable to pass a physical.<ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/adam-shaheen-trade-to-texans-off-following-failed-physical-te-returns-dolphins|title=Adam Shaheen trade to Texans off following failed physical; TE returns to Dolphins|date=August 11, 2022|accessdate=August 11, 2022|first=Eric|last=Edholm}}</ref> The Dolphins placed him on injured reserve on August 16.<ref>{{cite web|work=MiamiDolphins.com|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-roster-moves-x3672|title=Dolphins make roster moves|date=August 16, 2022|accessdate=August 17, 2022}}</ref>

'''Adam Bisnowaty''' (born December 14, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]] as a four-year starter at [[left tackle]], and was first-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference football teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]] his last two seasons. He played in the NFL for the [[New York Giants]].

==Early life==
Bisnowaty was born in [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]], and is Jewish.<ref name=autogenerated1>Nolan Nawrocki (2017). [https://books.google.com/books?id=rQ6bDgAAQBAJ&dq=adam+bisnowaty&pg=PT212 ''NFL Draft 2017''<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref>[http://kaplanskorner.com/2017/05/04/yes-nfl-draft-wait-theres/ "Yes, the NFL draft is over, but wait - there's more,"<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170505060808/http://kaplanskorner.com/2017/05/04/yes-nfl-draft-wait-theres/ |date=May 5, 2017 }} Kaplan's Korner.</ref> His parents are Miron and Randi Bisnowaty. He has a sister, Dana Bisnowaty.<ref name=autogenerated6>[http://pittsburghpanthers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=5410 "Adam Bisnowaty - 2016 Football Roster"<!-- Bot generated title -->], pittsburghpanthers.com.</ref> His father is Israeli-born, grew up in [[Rishon LeZion]], served in the [[Agaf HaModi'in]] (the military intelligence unit of the [[Israel Defense Forces]]), and came to the United States at the age of 27.<ref name=autogenerated9>[https://nypost.com/2017/07/24/meet-the-giant-who-wears-his-judaism-on-and-under-his-sleeve/ Meet the Giant who wears his Judaism on (and under) his sleeve<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref>[http://njjewishnews.com/kaplanskorner/2013/09/04/cleaning-out-the-in-box/ "Cleaning out the in-box,"]{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Kaplan's Korner.</ref><ref name=autogenerated5>[http://www.ynet.co.il/articles/0,7340,L-4961915,00.html "שחקן NFL מתוצרת כחול-לבן"], Ynet.</ref>  Adam's paternal grandmother is a [[Holocaust survivor]] who escaped the [[The Holocaust in Poland|Nazi]]s by hiding in the woods in Poland.<ref name=autogenerated9 />

Bisnowaty said: "I have a deep connection with Israel, my two parents are Jewish, my father is from Israel, and a large part of my family still lives there."<ref name=autogenerated5 /> He has a large Hebrew tattoo on his left arm, which translates to "I am what I am," which in the [[Old Testament]] God said to Moses when Moses asked what to call him.<ref>[https://www.jta.org/2017/08/04/life-religion/this-new-york-giants-player-shows-his-jewish-pride-on-and-off-the-field This New York Giants player shows his Jewish pride on and off the field | Jewish Telegraphic Agency<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref name=autogenerated9 />

Growing up, he preferred basketball, baseball, and wrestling to football.<ref name=autogenerated7>[http://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/football/story/_/id/7027282/adam-bisnowaty-four-star-ot-grew-love-football "Adam Bisnowaty, a four-star OT, grew to love football,"<!-- Bot generated title -->] ESPN.</ref> In seventh grade, he weighed {{convert|210|lb|kg}}, and in eighth grade he weighed {{convert|245|lb|kg}}, and with his size his attention soon shifted to football.<ref>[http://www.post-gazette.com/sports/high-school-football/2011/08/15/Blue-Chip-Chat-with-Adam-Bisnowaty-Fox-Chapel/stories/201108150197 "Blue Chip Chat with ... Adam Bisnowaty, Fox Chapel,"<!-- Bot generated title -->] ''Pittsburgh Post-Gazette''.</ref><ref name=autogenerated7 />

At [[Fox Chapel Area High School]] in Pennsylvania, Bisnowaty played [[offensive guard]] and [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|tackle]], was ranked the country's # 19 recruit by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]], and was a four-star recruit.<ref name=autogenerated6 /><ref name=autogenerated4>Ryan Palencer (2015). [https://books.google.com/books?id=8ZXGCQAAQBAJ&dq=adam+bisnowaty&pg=PA107 ''The Next Wave''<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref name=autogenerated3>[http://www.nj.com/giants/index.ssf/2017/05/5_things_to_know_about_giants_6th_round_pick_adam.html "5 things to know about Giants' 6th round pick Adam Bisnowaty, who plays with a mean streak,"<!-- Bot generated title -->] NJ.com.</ref><ref name=autogenerated2>[http://www.pennlive.com/pittsburgh-panthers/2017/04/adam_bisnowaty_nfl_draft_pitt.html "NFL Draft 2017: Pitt OT Adam Bisnowaty goes to the New York Giants in the sixth round,"<!-- Bot generated title -->] PennLive.com.</ref><ref>[http://fcasdathletics.org/latest-news/adam-bisnowatys-journey-nfl-big-apple/ "Adam Bisnowaty's Journey to the NFL and the Big Apple,"<!-- Bot generated title -->] Fox Chapel Area Athletics.</ref> He was named Pennsylvania Football News All-Class AAAA, and all-conference at [[defensive tackle]].<ref name=autogenerated6 /> He also competed in wrestling for the high school, and in [[track and field]]—throwing [[discus]], [[javelin]], and [[shot put]] (for which he holds the school record at 43' 7").<ref name=autogenerated6 /><ref name=autogenerated7 /><ref>[https://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/SchoolRecords.aspx?SchoolID=6431 "Fox Chapel HS Track Records,"<!-- Bot generated title -->] athletic.net.</ref>

==College career==
Bisnowaty played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]], choosing them over Florida and 12 other offers.<ref name=autogenerated4 /><ref name=autogenerated3 /> He earned an undergraduate degree from Pittsburgh in communications in 2015, and a master's degree in health and fitness.<ref name=autogenerated4 /><ref name=autogenerated3 /><ref>[http://triblive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/sports/highschool/s_779594.html "Fox Chapel star Bisnowaty makes it official with Pitt,"<!-- Bot generated title -->] ''Pittsburgh Tribune''.</ref> All-America

In 2012, he [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]]ed.<ref name=autogenerated3 />  Subsequently, Bisnowaty was a four-year starter at [[left tackle]].<ref name=autogenerated3 />  He was named to the ''[[Jewish Sports Review]]'' 2014 College Football [[All-America]] Offensive Team.<ref>[http://www.jewishsportsreview.com/2014FBAAOT.html "2014 College Football All-America Offensive Team,"<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170930035908/http://www.jewishsportsreview.com/2014FBAAOT.html |date=September 30, 2017 }} ''Jewish Sports Review''.</ref> He was a First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference football teams|All-Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) selection in each of his final seasons, and was named to the All-ACC Academic team for four consecutive years.<ref name=autogenerated3 /> As a senior in 2016 he started every game at left tackle.<ref name=autogenerated2 /> He finished his college career with 43 starts in 45 games.<ref name=autogenerated6 />

===New York Giants===

'''Adam Redmond''' (born May 19, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] as an undrafted [[free agent]] after the [[2016 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Harvard Crimson football|Harvard Crimson]].

==Early life==
Redmond attended [[Walsh Jesuit High School]], where he received Division Two All-district honors in his last 2 years as a starter at [[offensive tackle]] and [[long snapper]]. He accepted a football scholarship from [[Harvard University]]. As a sophomore in 2013, he started 9 games at [[left tackle]].

As a junior in 2014, he started all 10 games at [[left tackle]] and received honorable-mention [[Ivy League|All-Ivy League]] honors. As a senior in 2015, he started all 10 games at [[Center (American football)|center]] and was named first-team  [[Ivy League|All-Ivy League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/article/20160408/NEWS/304089209|title=Browns notebook: Walsh Jesuit grad Adam Redmond among local NFL hopefuls to work out for hometown team next week|website=beaconjournal.com|accessdate=May 2, 2021}}</ref> He played a total of 31 career games and studied sociology.

'''Adam Oneal Butler''' (born April 12, 1994) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive tackle]] for the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt Commodores]]. Butler signed with the [[New England Patriots]] as an [[Free agent#National Football League (NFL)|undrafted free agent]] after the [[2017 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Butler, a descendant of [[children's rights]] campaigner [[Edna Gladney]], attended [[Duncanville High School]] in [[Duncanville, Texas]]. After starting at defensive end as a sophomore, he moved to left tackle, where he started as a junior and senior. He was a two-time captain of the Duncanville Panthers football team, earning MVP honors his senior season, a season in which he blocked eight field goal attempts in addition to serving as the team’s starting left tackle.<ref> https://vucommodores.com/roster/adam-butler/ </ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.patriots.com/team/players/roster/adam-butler|title=Adam Butler (profile)|website=Patriots.com|access-date=September 10, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170910052553/http://www.patriots.com/team/players/roster/adam-butler|archive-date=September 10, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

A 3-star offensive guard recruit, Butler committed to [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt]] to play college football over offers from [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa]], [[North Texas Mean Green football|North Texas]], [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football|Oklahoma State]], and [[Wyoming Cowboys football|Wyoming]].<ref> https://247sports.com/player/adam-butler-7551/high-school-15617/</ref>

==College career==
Butler [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his freshman year at Vanderbilt. Going into his redshirt freshman season, he was moved from the offensive line to the defensive line.
He played both defensive tackle and defensive end throughout his college career.<ref> https://vucommodores.com/roster/adam-butler/ </ref> In four seasons for Vanderbilt, Butler played in 48 games with 35 starts, accumulating 113 total [[tackled gridiron|tackles]], 10 [[qb sack|sacks]], two blocked [[extra point]]s, and one defensive [[touchdown]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.vucommodores.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/adam_butler_807657.html|title=Adam Butler (profile)|website=VUCommodores.com|access-date=September 10, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170910172836/http://www.vucommodores.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/adam_butler_807657.html|archive-date=September 10, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref> https://vucommodores.com/roster/adam-butler/</ref>

===New England Patriots===
Butler signed with the [[New England Patriots]] as an undrafted free agent on May 5, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots Sign Sixth-Round Draft Pick Conor McDermott; Sign 19 Rookie Free Agents|url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/05/05/patriots-sign-sixth-round-draft-pick-conor-mcdermott-sign-19-rookie-free-agents|website=Patriots.com|date=May 5, 2017|access-date=September 13, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170512003817/http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/05/05/patriots-sign-sixth-round-draft-pick-conor-mcdermott-sign-19-rookie-free-agents|archive-date=May 12, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> After impressing in the Patriots' [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]] and preseason that summer, he earned a spot on the Patriots' 53-man roster.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://nesn.com/2017/09/how-patriots-rookie-adam-butler-found-out-he-made-initial-53-man-roster/|title=How Patriots Rookie Adam Butler Found Out He Made Initial 53-Man Roster|author=Kyed, Doug|website=NESN.com|date=September 6, 2017|access-date=September 10, 2017}}</ref> He was active for the Patriots' regular season home opener, seeing 21 snaps and recording a tackle in a 42–27 loss to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-england-patriots/post/_/id/4805578/mike-gillislees-usage-shows-how-hes-patriots-top-option-as-power-rb|title=Mike Gillislee's usage shows how he's Patriots' top option as power RB|author=Reiss, Mike|website=ESPN.com|date=September 9, 2017|access-date=September 10, 2017}}</ref> The Patriots made it to [[Super Bowl LII]], but came up short to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] by a score of 41–33; Butler recorded 1 tackle. The Patriots made it back to the Super Bowl the following season, where they defeated the [[Los Angeles Rams]] 13–3 in [[Super Bowl LIII]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.heraldnews.com/sports/20190208/super-bowl-season-ringing-endorsement-for-patriots-butler |title=Super Bowl season a ringing endorsement for Patriots' Butler - Sports - the Herald News, Fall River, MA - Fall River, MA |access-date=February 16, 2019 |archive-date=February 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190217030528/https://www.heraldnews.com/sports/20190208/super-bowl-season-ringing-endorsement-for-patriots-butler |url-status=dead }}</ref>
In Week 2 of the 2019 season against the [[Miami Dolphins]], Butler recorded 2 sacks as the Patriots won 43–0.<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 September 2019 |title=Newcomer Brown scores as Patriots beat Dolphins 43–0 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127862 |access-date=15 September 2019 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>
In Week 8 against the [[Cleveland Browns]], Butler recorded a team-high 2 sacks on quarterback [[Baker Mayfield]] in the 27–13 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 October 2019 |title=Belichick wins 300th, perfect Patriots beat Browns 27–13 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127895 |access-date=27 October 2019 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

Butler re-signed on a one-year [[restricted free agent]] contract with the Patriots on April 17, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Patriots Sign Restricted Free Agent DL Adam Butler |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-restricted-free-agent-dl-adam-butler |website=Patriots.com |date=April 17, 2020 |access-date=April 18, 2020 |archive-date=April 22, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200422060906/https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-restricted-free-agent-dl-adam-butler |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On March 18, 2021, Butler signed a two-year contract with the Dolphins.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-sign-dl-adam-butler|title= Miami Dolphins Sign DL Adam Butler |work=MiamiDolphins.com|date=March 18, 2021}}</ref> On August 2, 2022, Butler was released because of a failed physical.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Move: Dolphins release Butler|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/roster-move-dolphins-release-butler |website=Miamidolphins.com|date=August 2, 2022}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On January 27, 2023, Butler signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williamson |first=Bill |date=January 27, 2023 |title=Raiders sign defensive lineman Adam Butler |url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2023/1/27/23574964/raiders-news-adam-butler-sign-defensive-lineman |access-date=2023-10-31 |website=Silver and Black Pride |publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> He played all 17 games, recording 28 tackles, five sacks, four passes defensed, and a forced fumble.

On March 18, 2024, Butler re-signed with the Raiders.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders re-sign defensive tackles Adam Butler and John Jenkins|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-re-sign-defensive-tackles-john-jenkins-and-adam-butler-nfl-2024-free-agency|website=Raiders.com|date=March 18, 2024}}</ref> He played in every game and recorded a career-high 65 tackles and five sacks.

On March 12, 2025, Butler re-signed with the Raiders on a three-year, $16.5 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Raiders sign DT Adam Butler|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-adam-butler-defensive-tackle-nfl-2025-free-agency-transactions|access-date=March 13, 2025|website=raiders.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''Adam Pankey''' (born February 2, 1994) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]]. He played [[college football]] at [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia]].

===Green Bay Packers (first stint)===
Pankey signed with the [[Green Bay Packers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on May 5, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign five draft picks, 15 rookie free agents|url=http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-press-release/article-1/Packers-sign-five-draft-picks-15-rookie-free-agents/59429000-4dd0-49bc-a103-9df1aef245a2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180505201404/http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-press-release/article-1/Packers-sign-five-draft-picks-15-rookie-free-agents/59429000-4dd0-49bc-a103-9df1aef245a2|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 5, 2018|website=Packers.com|date=May 5, 2017|access-date=October 27, 2017}}</ref> He was waived by the Packers on September 2, 2017 and was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers announce roster moves to reduce roster to 53|url=http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-roster-moves/article-1/Packers-announce-roster-moves-to-reduce-roster-to-53/94349c91-be80-4c10-b860-36a5a83c78cd|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180507085345/http://www.packers.com/news-and-events/article-roster-moves/article-1/Packers-announce-roster-moves-to-reduce-roster-to-53/94349c91-be80-4c10-b860-36a5a83c78cd|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 7, 2018|website=Packers.com|date=September 2, 2017|access-date=October 27, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign LB Brooks, claim LB Odom, place OL Barclay on IR|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-lb-brooks-claim-lb-odom-place-ol-barclay-on-ir-19311378|website=Packers.com|date=September 3, 2017|access-date=October 27, 2017}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 13, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign G/T Adam Pankey to active roster, G Darrell Greene to practice squad|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-g-t-adam-pankey-to-active-roster-g-darrell-greene-to-pract-19365622|website=Packers.com|date=September 13, 2017|access-date=October 27, 2017}}</ref>

Pankey was re-signed on March 13, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/green-bay-packers/article/nfl-free-agency-packers-tender-offensive-lineman-adam-pankey--116192054/|title=Report: Packers tender OL Adam Pankey|date=March 13, 2018|work=247sports.com}}</ref> He was waived on September 1, 2018 and was signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers announce roster moves|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-announce-roster-moves-1|website=Packers.com|date=September 1, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign eight players to practice squad|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-eight-players-to-practice-squad|website=Packers.com|date=September 2, 2018|access-date=September 3, 2018|archive-date=September 3, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180903215310/https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-eight-players-to-practice-squad|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 8, 2018<ref>{{cite web |title=Packers sign G/T Adam Pankey to active roster |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-g-t-adam-pankey-to-active-roster |website=Packers.com |access-date=December 8, 2018 |date=December 8, 2018}}</ref> and saw playing time the next day in a 34–20 victory over the [[Atlanta Falcons]].

On August 31, 2019, Pankey was waived by the Packers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-announce-roster-moves-x5219|title=Packers announce roster moves|date=August 31, 2019|website=Packers.com}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On September 2, 2019, Pankey was signed to the [[Tennessee Titans]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Wrap up Practice Squad By Adding Former Packers OL Adam Pankey|url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-add-qb-logan-woodside-eight-others-to-team-s-practice-squad|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TitansOnline.com|date=September 2, 2019}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers (second stint)===
On September 21, 2019, Pankey was signed by the Packers off the Titans practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=G Lane Taylor placed on injured reserve; G/T Adam Pankey signed from Titans' practice squad|url=https://www.packers.com/news/g-lane-taylor-placed-on-ir-g-t-adam-pankey-signed-from-titans-ps|website=Packers.com|date=September 21, 2019}}</ref> He was waived on December 9, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers activate T Jared Veldheer|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-activate-t-jared-veldheer|website=Packers.com|date=December 9, 2019|access-date=December 10, 2019|archive-date=December 10, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210014529/https://www.packers.com/news/packers-activate-t-jared-veldheer|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On December 10, 2019, Pankey was claimed off waivers by the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Make Roster Moves On Tuesday|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-roster-moves-on-tuesday|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=December 10, 2019}}</ref>

===New York Jets===

'''Aaron Phillip Stinnie''' (born February 18, 1994) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for the [[New York Giants]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[James Madison Dukes football|James Madison Dukes]]. He has previously played in the NFL for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].

==Early life==
Stinnie was born and grew up in [[Charlottesville, Virginia]] and attended [[St. Anne's-Belfield School]]. He focused on basketball and did not begin playing [[high school football|football]] until his junior year after joining the team at the insistence of his friends.<ref name="block">{{Cite news |last=O'Connor |first=John |date=October 10, 2017 |title=JMU's Aaron Stinnie, a relatively new kid on the block, drawing NFL scouts' attention |work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]] |url=https://www.richmond.com/sports/college/schools/james-madison/jmu-s-aaron-stinnie-a-relatively-new-kid-on-the/article_d50e742c-fb98-5026-a3d9-59ff41f830b0.html |access-date=September 9, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
After [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his freshman season, Stinnie began his career with the [[James Madison Dukes football|Dukes]] as a defensive lineman, recording 11 tackles and 1.5 sacks in 12 games in his first season of playing time, before moving over to the offensive line going into his redshirt sophomore season. Stinnie became a three-year starter for JMU, starting 42 consecutive games to end his career, and was an [[Football Championship Subdivision|FCS]] [[College Football All-America Team|All-America]] selection for his redshirt junior and senior seasons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Madia |first=Greg |date=March 21, 2018 |title=Stinnie Keeping Dream Alive |url=https://jamesmadison.rivals.com/news/stinnie-keeping-dream-alive/printable |access-date=October 30, 2018 |website=DukesofJMU.com |publisher=[[Rivals.com]]}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
Stinnie signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on April 28, 2018, and made the final 53-man roster out of training camp.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wolf |first=Jason |date=April 29, 2018 |title=Titans signing more than 20 undrafted free agents |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/nfl/titans/2018/04/28/titans-signing-undrafted-free-agents/561298002/ |access-date=October 30, 2018 |website=[[The Tennessean]] |publisher=USA Today Network}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2018 |title=Former STAB/JMU standout Aaron Stinnie makes Tennessee Titans roster |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cvillevarsity/former-stab-jmu-standout-aaron-stinnie-makes-tennessee-titans-roster/article_ed3bb082-ae38-11e8-8b7c-df6a58a4ad23.html |access-date=September 28, 2018 |website=[[The Daily Progress]]}}</ref> Stinnie made his NFL debut, the only regular season appearance of his rookie season, on October 21, 2018, against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 14, 2018 |title=Titans-Ravens Game Notes |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-ravens-game-notes |access-date=October 30, 2018 |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref>

On August 31, 2019, Stinnie was waived by the Titans and was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=August 31, 2019 |title=Roster Moves: Titans Trim Roster to 53 Players While Also Trading WR Taywan Taylor to Browns |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/roster-moves-titans-trim-roster-to-53-players-while-also-trading-wr-taywan-taylo |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=September 1, 2019 |title=Titans Add QB Logan Woodside, Eight Others to Team's Practice Squad |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-add-qb-logan-woodside-eight-others-to-team-s-practice-squad |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 7, 2019, before the season opener.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=September 7, 2019 |title=Titans Promote OL Aaron Stinnie to 53-Man Roster, Waive WR Kalif Raymond |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-promote-ol-aaron-stinnie-to-53-man-roster-waive-wr-kalif-raymond |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref> He was waived on November 9.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=November 9, 2019 |title=Titans Promote WR Cody Hollister to 53-Man Roster, Waive OL Aaron Stinnie |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-promote-wr-cody-hollister-to-53-man-roster-waive-ol-aaron-stinnie |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On November 11, 2019, Stinnie was claimed off waivers by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=November 11, 2019 |title=Bucs Claim G Aaron Stinnie Off Waivers |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-claim-guard-aaron-stinnie-off-waivers-roster-move-2019 |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=Buccaneers.com |archive-date=May 18, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210518133137/https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-claim-guard-aaron-stinnie-off-waivers-roster-move-2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Stinnie appeared in five games, three with the Titans and two with the Buccaneers, during the 2019 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Stinnie 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/StinAa00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=January 10, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Stinnie appeared in six games during the 2020 regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Willett |first=Preston |date=January 11, 2021 |title=STAB alum Aaron Stinnie to start in NFL Playoffs |url=https://www.cbs19news.com/story/43155525/stab-alum-aaron-stinnie-to-start-in-nfl-playoffs |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=cbs19news.com}}</ref> Stinnie made his first professional start in the divisional round of the playoffs against the [[New Orleans Saints]] after starting right guard [[Alex Cappa]] fractured his ankle in the wild-card round.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Knight |first=Joey |date=January 15, 2021 |title=Can Bucs guard Aaron Stinnie go from healthy scratch to heady starter? |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/bucs/2021/01/15/can-bucs-guard-aaron-stinnie-go-from-healthy-scratch-to-heady-starter/ |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=[[Tampa Bay Times]]}}</ref> He started the final three games of the playoffs, including [[Super Bowl LV]] as the Buccaneers beat the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shiers |first=Mike |date=February 7, 2021 |title=Charlottesville-native Aaron Stinnie is a Super Bowl Champion |url=https://www.nbc29.com/2021/02/08/charlottesville-native-aaron-stinnie-is-super-bowl-champion/ |access-date=March 16, 2021 |website=nbc29.com}}</ref>

Stinnie signed a contract extension with the Buccaneers on March 17, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |author=Smith, Scott |title=Bucs Re-Sign Playoff Standout Aaron Stinnie |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/guard-aaron-stinnie-re-signs-2021-buccaneers |website=Buccaneers.com |date=March 17, 2021 |access-date=March 17, 2021}}</ref> He made his first career regular season start in Week 12 in place of an injured [[Ali Marpet]]. He suffered a knee injury in that game and was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 1, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Easterling |first=Luke |date=2021-12-01 |title=Bucs place G Aaron Stinnie on injured reserve |url=https://bucswire.usatoday.com/2021/12/01/nfl-news-tampa-bay-buccaneers-aaron-stinnie-injured-reserve/ |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=Bucs Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> He was activated on January 8, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=January 8, 2022 |title=Grayson Promotion, Stinnie Activation Among Saturday Moves |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-grayson-promotion-stinnie-activation-week-18-roster-moves |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> In the 2021 season, he appeared in six games and started one.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Stinnie 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/StinAa00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 13, 2022, Stinnie re-signed with the Buccaneers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=March 13, 2022 |title=Bucs Re-Sign Aaron Stinnie |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/aaron-stinnie-sign-free-agency-2022-roster-move |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> He suffered a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] in the preseason and was placed on injured reserve on August 22, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=August 22, 2022 |title=Bucs Place Cam Gill, Aaron Stinnie on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-place-cam-gill-aaron-stinnie-injured-reserve-2022-roster-moves |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref>

On March 15, 2023, Stinnie re-signed with the Buccaneers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=March 15, 2023 |title=Bucs Agree to Terms with G Aaron Stinnie |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/aaron-stinnie-agree-terms-tampa-bay-buccaneers-free-agency-2023 |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> He appeared in 13 games and started 11 in the 2023 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Stinnie 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/StinAa00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On March 15, 2024, Stinnie signed with the [[New York Giants]].<ref name="g218">{{cite web | last=Traina | first=Patricia | title=New York Giants Add Two Interior O-linemen | website=SI.com | date=2024-03-15 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/giants/gm-report/new-york-giants-add-two-interior-o-linemen | access-date=2024-12-17}}</ref> He was named a backup guard, starting three games at left guard as an injury fill-in.

'''Adam Choice''' (born November 30, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson Tigers]].

==Early life==
Choice attended [[Thomas County Central High School]] in [[Thomasville, Georgia]]. During his [[high school football]] career, he had over 5,000 rushing yards playing at the quarterback position. He committed to [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]] to play college football at the running back position.

==College career==
As a true freshman at [[Clemson University]] in 2014, Choice played in six games, rushing for 218 yards on 50 carries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Choice College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/adam-choice-1.html |access-date=November 14, 2023 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> However, on October 18, 2014, Choice suffered a season ending torn ACL at Boston College. Choice was redshirted the following year. Choice returned as a reserve running back for the 2016–2018 seasons finishing his college career with 1,250 rushing yards on 239 carries and 14 touchdowns. Choice earned a master's degree in human resource development.

==Professional career==
Choice was signed as an undrafted free agent by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on May 3, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign 12 Undrafted Rookie Free Agents|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-12-undrafted-rookie-free-agents|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=May 3, 2019|accessdate=May 21, 2019}}</ref> He was waived/injured on May 29, 2019, and placed on injured reserve.<ref name="o219">{{cite web | last=Boyle | first=John | title=Seahawks Sign RB Marcelias Sutton, Waive/Injured RB Adam Choice | website=Seahawks.com | date=2019-05-29 | url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-rb-marcelias-sutton-waive-injured-rb-adam-choice | access-date=2024-10-22}}</ref> He was waived on May 4, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=May 4, 2020 |title=Seahawks Sign 12 Undrafted Rookie Free Agents; Waive Four Players |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-12-undrafted-rookie-free-agents-waive-four-players |access-date=November 14, 2023 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Choice is the cousin of former NFL running backs [[Tashard Choice]] and [[Joe Burns (American football)|Joe Burns]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clemsontigers.com/sports/football/roster/adam-choice|title=Clemson Bio|website=clemsontigers.com}}</ref>

'''Abdullah Anderson Jr.''' (born January 24, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Bucknell Bison football|Bucknell Bison]]. Anderson signed with the [[Chicago Bears]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2018 and spent three seasons with them before playing with several other NFL teams.

==Early life==
Anderson was born in [[Atlantic City, New Jersey]], on January 24, 1996. He grew up in nearby [[Galloway Township]] and attended [[Absegami High School]].<ref>Gill, Mike. [https://973espn.com/absegami-grad-abdullah-anderson-heading-to-windy-city/ "Absegami Grad Abdullah Anderson Heading to Windy City"], [[WPEN (FM)]], April 28, 2018. Retrieved September 28, 2019. "The Galloway Township product had a very good showing at the NFL combine, allowing him to jump on NFL teams radar, getting workouts with multiple teams including the Seahawks and 49ers... He was the 2017 Patriot League Defensive Player of the Year, and in 43 career games, the 2014 Absegami alum accumulated 171 tackles, 33.5 tackles for a loss, 15.5 sacks and four blocked kicks."</ref> He is the only son of Abdullah Anderson Sr. and Octavia Anderson. Anderson has one older sister, Amira.<ref name="Bucknell bio" />  Anderson, who had played youth football, decided for his senior year it was time to tell Braves coach Dennis Scuderi Jr. that he might like to finish out his prep career with one season of football. Anderson went on to have a good enough season to catch the eye of Bucknell University coach Joe Susan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-01-10 |title=Former Absegami basketball star Abdullah Anderson hoping for a shot at the NFL - South Jersey Glory Days |url=https://sjglorydays.com/former-absegami-basketball-star-abdullah-anderson-hoping-for-a-shot-at-the-nfl/ |access-date=2024-08-27 |website=sjglorydays.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Quite a turn of events for a kid who thought he was going to play college basketball. Anderson disciplined his body and weight and went from 235 as a senior in high school to 300 pounds in his college career.

==College career==
Anderson attended [[Bucknell Bison football|Bucknell]], where he majored in economics. As a freshman, he started all 11 games at defensive tackle; he was one of five defensive players to start every game and the only freshman on team to do so.<ref name="Bucknell bio"<ref name="Bucknell bio">{{cite web|url=https://bucknellbison.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3595|title=Abdullah Anderson|work=[[Bucknell Bison]]|accessdate=September 26, 2019}}</ref>

During his second year in 2015, Anderson was one of six defensive players to start all 11 games and one of three defensive linemen to start every game. He totaled 46 tackles, eight tackles for loss, 4.5 sacks and three pass breakups from defensive tackle position. He ranked seventh on team in tackles and fifth on squad in tackles for loss.<ref name="Bucknell bio" />

In his junior season, Anderson started all 11 games on the defensive line for a third straight year. He ranked fourth on team with 55 tackles, 13.5 tackles for loss, five pass breakups and two blocked kicks. Anderson ranked second in the [[Patriot League]] in tackles for loss and ranked third in Patriot League in sacks. He was named Patriot League Defensive Player of the Week on November 21 after totaling five tackles, 3.5 tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, one pass breakup and two blocked field goals against [[Fordham Rams football|Fordham]].<ref name="Bucknell bio" />

During his senior year in 2017, Anderson recorded 42 tackles, nine tackles for loss, 2.5 sacks, two fumble recoveries, an interception, and blocked an extra point. In addition to being named All-Patriot League for the fourth time, he was named the 2017 Patriot League Defensive Player of the Year and [[NCAA FCS]] Collegiate Player of the Year by the Brooks-Irvine Memorial Football Club.<ref name="Anderson signs with Bears">{{cite web|url=https://bucknellbison.com/news/2018/4/28/211713858.aspx|title=Bucknell's Abdullah Anderson Signs with Chicago Bears|work=[[Bucknell Bison]]|date=April 28, 2018|accessdate=September 26, 2019}}</ref> He was also named second-team [[All-American]] by the [[Associated Press]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dailyitem.com/sports/bucknell-s-anderson-signed-to-bears-practice-squad/article_e2a2916a-b052-11e8-8566-43fb8407bf4d.html|title=Bucknell's Anderson signed to Bears' practice squad|newspaper=[[The Daily Item (Sunbury)|The Daily Item]]|date=September 28, 2018|accessdate=September 26, 2019}}</ref>

Anderson ended his college career with 43 starts in which he had 171 tackles, 33.5 tackles for loss, 15.5 sacks, and a school-record four blocked kicks.<ref name="Anderson signs with Bears" />

'''Adam M. Prentice''' (born January 16, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] for the [[Denver Broncos]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Colorado State Rams football|Colorado State Rams]] and [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]] and was signed by the Broncos as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2021. He has also played for the [[New Orleans Saints]].

In addition to his usage as a fullback, Prentice has also occasionally played [[running back]] (halfback/tailback), often playing running back either as a situational ballcarrier or a pass blocker/pass protector. 

==Early life==
Prentice was born in Fresno on January 16, 1997, to Renae and Gary Prentice. He graduated from [[Clovis High School (California)|Clovis High]] in 2015, receiving the Bnai Brith award from Fresno County for his outstanding community service, excelling academically, in track, wrestling, and football. Prentice would place 5th in the Valley in the shot put, 2nd in the state in wrestling, and was the Fresno Bee defensive player of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boogaard |first=Andy |date=May 19, 2015 |title=Clovis' Adam Prentice named B'nai B'rith winner in emotional night |url=https://www.fresnobee.com/sports/high-school/article21354240.html |access-date=October 9, 2023 |website=Fresno Bee}}</ref> Prentice would lose his father Gary suddenly to cancer his senior year at Clovis High. The memory of his father would inspire Prentice throughout college.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mellon |first=Brianna |date=November 28, 2020 |title=Good Sports: Former Clovis Cougar Adam Prentice playing his 6th year of college football at South Carolina |url=https://abc30.com/good-sports-adam-prentice/8315700/ |access-date=October 9, 2023 |website=ABC30 Fresno}}</ref>

==College career==
Prentice began his collegiate career at [[Colorado State Rams football|Colorado State]]. He join the team as a walk-on and [[redshirted]] his true freshman season. Prentice was named the Rams' starting fullback and awarded a scholarship before suffering a season-ending injury shortly before the start of his redshirt freshman season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lyell |first=Kelly |date=August 26, 2016 |title=CSU loses starting fullback to season-ending injury |url=https://www.coloradoan.com/story/sports/csu/football/2016/08/26/csu-loses-starting-fullback-season-ending-injury/89413916/ |access-date=September 1, 2021 |website=The Coloradoan |language=en-US}}</ref> Prentice served as Colorado State's primary fullback for the next three seasons before transferring to South Carolina as a graduate transfer.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bezjak |first=Lou |date=December 30, 2019 |title=South Carolina adds another grad transfer from Colorado State, this time a fullback |url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-football/article238837453.html |access-date=October 9, 2023 |website=TheState.com}}</ref> At South Carolina Prentice was named Offensive Player of the game in their historic victory vs Auburn. Prentice finished his masters in structural engineering at South Carolina.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kendall |first=Josh |date=October 21, 2020 |title=South Carolina's unlikely offensive star: Adam Prentice excels in the dirty work |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2150521/2020/10/21/south-carolinas-unlikely-offensive-star-adam-prentice-excels-in-the-dirty-work/ |access-date=October 9, 2023 |website=The Athletic}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos (first stint)===
Prentice was signed by the [[Denver Broncos]] as an undrafted free agent on May 3, 2021.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Trickel |first=Erick |date=May 3, 2021 |title=Broncos' 11 Undrafted Free Agents: What Fans Need to Know |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/broncos/news/denver-broncos-11-undrafted-free-agents-breakdown |access-date=September 1, 2021 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> He was waived by the Broncos on August 31.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=August 31, 2021 |title=Broncos make series of roster transactions to reach 53-man limit |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-make-series-of-roster-transactions-to-reach-53-man-limit |access-date=October 9, 2023 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
Prentice was claimed off of waivers by the [[New Orleans Saints]] on September 1, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Luke |date=September 1, 2021 |title=Saints claim fullback Adam Prentice off waivers from Denver |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/article_cb0d47aa-0b41-11ec-8d6b-df73b802effe.html |access-date=September 1, 2021 |website=NOLA.com |language=en}}</ref> He was waived on September 14, and re-signed to the [[practice squad]]. Prentice was elevated to the active roster on November 25, for the team's Week 12 game against the [[Buffalo Bills]] and made his NFL debut in the game, starting at fullback and catching a pass from [[Trevor Siemian]] for ten yards for his first career reception.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Just |first=Amie |date=November 25, 2021 |title=Saints re-sign Will Clapp, elevate 2 players from practice squad |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/article_cbf2a340-4e44-11ec-bf4a-bf514ccda56c.html |access-date=November 26, 2021 |website=[[NOLA.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Buffalo Bills at New Orleans Saints - November 25th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202111250nor.htm |access-date=December 18, 2022 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was signed to the active roster on December 2.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 2, 2021 |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves ahead of Dallas Cowboys game {{!}} NFL Week 13 |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-announce-roster-moves-ahead-of-dallas-cowboys-game-nfl-week-1 |access-date=October 9, 2023 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref> As a rookie, Prentice recorded 3 rushing attempts for 5 yards, 3 receptions on 3 targets for 16 yards, and 1 tackle. He appeared in 7 games and started 3. 

Prentice made the Saints final roster in 2022, but was waived on October 1, 2022, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 1, 2022 |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-announce-roster-moves-nfl-week-4 |access-date=October 9, 2023 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on November 10.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 10, 2022 |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-announce-roster-moves-trevor-penning-111022 |access-date=October 9, 2023 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref> In 2022, Prentice recorded 4 rushing attempts for 9 yards, 3 receptions on 3 targets for 9 yards, 3 tackles, with 1 fumble. 

On October 14, 2023, Prentice was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 14, 2023 |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-announce-roster-moves-101423 |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref> He was reactivated on November 11, waived three days later, and re-signed to the practice squad on November 16.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 11, 2023 |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-announce-roster-moves-x5999 |access-date=November 14, 2023 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 14, 2023 |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-roster-moves-announced-kirkwood-111423 |access-date=November 14, 2023 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref><ref name="f608">{{cite web  | title=New Orleans Saints sign fullback Adam Prentice to practice squad | website=NewOrleansSaints.com | date=2023-11-16 | url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/adam-prentice-new-orleans-saints-fullback-practice-squad-roster-moves-111623 | access-date=2024-12-18}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 9.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 9, 2023 |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-announce-roster-moves-12-9-2023 |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref> In 2023, Prentice recorded 2 rushing attempts for 12 yards,  caught 2 of 3 targets for 12 receiving yards, 5 tackles, and 1 fumble. Prentice played in 13 games with 1 start in the 2023 season. 

In the 2024 season Prentice recorded 0 receptions on 4 targets and recorded a career-high 7 tackles. He appeared in 17 games with 7 starts.

=== Denver Broncos (second stint) ===
[[File:Adam Prentice Broncos.png|thumb|Prentice with the Broncos in 2025]]
On August 17, 2025, Prentice was signed by the Denver Broncos once again following injuries to fullbacks [[Michael Burton (American football)|Michael Burton]] and [[Nate Adkins]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Heath |first=Jon |title=Broncos bring back familiar face after 2 injuries at fullback |url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/broncos/2025/08/17/broncos-news-adam-prentice-signs-fullback-injuries/85701569007/ |access-date=2025-08-17 |website=Broncos Wire |language=}}</ref> On August 26, he was released.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=2025-08-26 |title=Broncos make series of transactions to reach 53-player roster limit |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-make-series-of-transactions-to-reach-53-player-roster-limit |access-date=2025-08-27 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref> The next day, he was re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=2025-08-27 |title=Broncos sign 16 players to practice squad |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-16-players-to-practice-squad |access-date=2025-08-28 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref> With both Burton and Adkins out with injury, Prentice was elevated from the practice squad for the team's first three games of the season.<ref name=":17">{{Cite web |last=Klis |first=Mike |date=2024-09-06 |title=Broncos place Malcolm Roach on short-term IR, promote Sam Ehlinger |url=https://www.9news.com/article/sports/nfl/denver-broncos/mike-klis/malcolm-roach-injured-reserve-sam-ehlinger-promoted/73-d3224dd4-6db4-4430-a961-a63084cbf541 |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=9news.com}}</ref> On September 24, he was promoted to the active roster.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=2025-09-24 |title=Broncos promote FB Adam Prentice to active roster |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-promote-fb-adam-prentice-to-active-roster |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref>

On March 12, 2026, Prentice re-signed with the Broncos on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |last1=DiLalla |first1=Aric |title=Broncos re-sign FB Adam Prentice to 1-year contract |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-re-sign-fb-adam-prentice-to-1-year-contract |website=DenverBroncos.com |access-date=13 March 2026}}</ref>

'''Abraham''' "'''Abe'''" '''Lucas''' (born October 25, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Seattle Seahawks]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Washington State Cougars football|Washington State Cougars]].

==Early life==
Lucas grew up in [[Everett, Washington]] and attended [[Archbishop Murphy High School]], where he played basketball and was an offensive and defensive lineman on the football team.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lawson |first=Theo |date=August 13, 2021 |title=Everett native makes prestigious college football watch list |url=https://www.heraldnet.com/sports/everett-native-makes-prestigious-college-football-watch-list/ |access-date=March 10, 2022 |work=[[The Everett Herald]]}}</ref> [[Kyler Gordon]] from the [[Chicago Bears]] was also a high school teammate of Lucas. Lucas was rated a three-star recruit and committed to play [[college football]] at Washington State over offers from Oregon State and Wyoming.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/wsu-cougar-football/wsu-gets-commitment-from-archbishop-murphy-lineman-abraham-lucas/|title=Archbishop Murphy lineman Abraham Lucas committed to Washington State|work=[[The Seattle Times]]|date=August 3, 2016|access-date=March 10, 2022}}</ref>

==College career==
Lucas [[redshirted]] his true freshman season at Washington State.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/2018/08/18/redshirt-freshmen-ready/|title=Redshirt freshmen ready for action after yearlong wait|work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=August 18, 2018|access-date=March 10, 2022}}</ref> He was named the Cougars' starting right tackle going into his redshirt freshman season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2018/nov/05/mike-leach-says-washington-state-rookie-abraham-lu/|title=Mike Leach says WSU rookie Abraham Lucas is 'one of the best offensive linemen' in Pac-12|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=November 5, 2018|access-date=March 10, 2022}}</ref> Lucas started all 13 of Washington State's games and was named second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|All-Pac-12 Conference]] and a freshman All-American by ''[[USA Today]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2018/dec/12/usa-today-tabs-washington-state-right-tackle-abrah/|title=USA Today tabs Washington State right tackle Abraham Lucas as Freshman All-American|work=[[The Spokesman-Review]]|date=December 12, 2018|access-date=March 10, 2022}}</ref> He started all of Washington State's games at right tackle as a redshirt sophomore and was again named second-team All-Pac-12.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.heraldnet.com/sports/archbishop-murphy-grad-abraham-lucas-earns-all-pac-12-honors/|title=Archbishop Murphy grad Abraham Lucas earns All-Pac-12 honors|work=[[The Everett Herald]]|date=December 10, 2019|access-date=March 10, 2022}}</ref> Lucas started all four games of Washington State's [[COVID-19]]-shortened [[2020 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2020 season]] and was named second-team All-Conference for a third straight season and was also named first-team All-Pac-12 by the [[Associated Press]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dnews.com/sports/wazzu-tackle-lucas-earns-first-team-all-pac-12-accolade/article_d48cf732-3a0c-51b6-af8b-2b71b16f9162.html|title=Wazzu tackle Lucas earns first-team All-Pac-12 accolade|work=[[Moscow-Pullman Daily News]]|date=December 26, 2020|access-date=March 10, 2022}}</ref> He considered entering the [[2021 NFL draft]], but opted to return to Washington State for a fifth season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/wsu-cougar-football/washington-states-abraham-lucas-puts-off-nfl-will-return-to-cougars-this-fall/|title=Washington State's Abraham Lucas puts off NFL, will return to Cougars this fall|work=[[The Seattle Times]]|date=January 19, 2021|access-date=March 10, 2022}}</ref> As a redshirt senior, Lucas started 12 games at right tackle and was named first-team All-Pac-12.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/wsu-cougar-football/wsus-max-borghi-abraham-lucas-and-jaylen-watson-opt-out-of-sun-bowl-to-prepare-for-nfl-draft/|title= WSU's Max Borghi, Abraham Lucas and ===Seattle Seahawks===
The [[Seattle Seahawks]] selected Lucas in the third round (72nd overall) in the [[2022 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/abraham-lucas-nfl-draft-offensive-lineman-washington-state |title=Seahawks Select Washington State OT Abraham Lucas With 72nd Overall Pick |date=April 29, 2022|website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He signed his rookie contract on May 26, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://seahawkswire.usatoday.com/2022/05/26/seahawks-tackle-abe-lucas-signs-rookie-contract/ |title=Seahawks tackle Abe Lucas signs his rookie contract |access-date=May 27, 2022 |date=May 26, 2022 |first=Liz |last=Matthews}}</ref> Lucas was named starting right tackle as a rookie, starting in 16 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abraham Lucas 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LucaAb00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 1 of the 2023 season, Lucas suffered a knee injury and was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign Offensive Tackles Raiqwon O'Neal & McClendon Curtis, Place Abraham Lucas On IR|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-offensive-tackles-raiqwon-o-neal-mcclendon-curtis-place-abraham-lu|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=September 13, 2023}}</ref> Lucas was activated off of injured reserve on November 30.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Activate T Abraham Lucas From Injured Reserve, Place G Phil Haynes On Injured Reserve|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-activate-t-abraham-lucas-from-injured-reserve-place-g-phil-haynes-on-in|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=November 30, 2023}}</ref> He appeared in and started six games in the 2023 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abraham Lucas 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LucaAb00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-12-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On July 18, 2024, Lucas was placed on the active/[[physically unable to perform]] (PUP) list, and was placed on reserves to begin the season.<ref name="u094">{{cite web | last=Boyle | first=John | title=Seahawks Place Seven On Physically Unable To Perform List Ahead Of 2024 Training Camp | website=Seahawks.com| date=2024-07-18 | url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-place-seven-on-physically-unable-to-perform-list-ahead-of-2024-training-camp | access-date=2024-11-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Make Roster Moves, Establish Initial 2024 53-Man Roster|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-make-roster-moves-establish-initial-2024-53-man-roster|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref> He was activated on November 13.<ref>{{cite web | last=Boyle | first=John | title=Seahawks Activate T Abraham Lucas From PUP List | website=Seahawks.com| date=2024-11-13 | url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-activate-t-abraham-lucas-from-pup-list | access-date=2025-06-21}}</ref> He appeared in and started seven games in the 2024 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abraham Lucas 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LucaAb00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On September 4, 2025, Lucas was signed to a three-year, $46 million extension.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=September 4, 2025 |title=Contract Extension A ‘Dream Come True’ For Seahawks Tackle Abraham Lucas |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/contract-extension-a-dream-come-true-for-seahawks-tackle-abraham-lucas |access-date=2025-09-04 |website=Seahawks.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He started in Super Bowl LX, a 29–13 win over the New England Patriots.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LX - Seattle Seahawks vs. New England Patriots - February 8th, 2026 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202602080nwe.htm |access-date=February 28, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Abdul Jabar Carter''' (born October 3, 2003) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[New York Giants]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]], earning [[unanimous All-American]] and [[Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year]] honors in 2024. Carter was selected by the Giants third overall in the [[2025 NFL draft]].

Carter was selected by the [[New York Giants]] with the third overall pick in the [[2025 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Salomone |first=Dan |date=April 24, 2025 |title=Giants select Abdul Carter with 3rd pick in 2025 NFL Draft |url=https://www.giants.com/news/abdul-carter-nfl-draft-edge-penn-state-nittany-lions |access-date=April 25, 2025 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> On May 22, 2025, Carter signed a four-year, $45.2 million contract that was fully-guaranteed.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2025/05/22/abdul-carter-contract-details-giants/83794607007/|work=USAToday.com|title=Giants sign first-round Abdul Carter pick to rookie deal|first=Nick|last=Brinkerhoff|date=May 22, 2025}}</ref>

Carter was disciplined for multiple games in his 2025 rookie season. Against the Packers in Week 11, Carter was benched for the opening series reportedly due to sleeping during a walk-through practice; Carter claimed he was instead getting treatment, and interim coach [[Mike Kafka]] declined to comment.<ref>{{cite news |last=Schefter |first=Adam |title=Missed practice an 'honest mistake,' says Giants' Abdul Carter |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/47009978/missed-practice-honest-mistake-says-giants-abdul-carter |work=[[ESPN]] |date=November 18, 2025 |access-date=May 29, 2026}}</ref> Against the Patriots in Week 13, Carter was benched for the entire first quarter after missing a meeting the previous week.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Carroll |first1=Charlotte |last2=Duggan |first2=Dan |title=Why Giants benched Abdul Carter for first series vs. Patriots: Sources |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6853903/2025/12/02/ny-giants-abdul-carter-benched-patriots/ |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=December 2, 2025 |access-date=May 29, 2026}}</ref>

Although Carter started the season slow with only half a sack and one tackle for loss through the first 12 games even though he played the majority of defensive snaps in each game, he finished the season strong with at least half a sack in each of his games in December. Carter finished fifth for the 2025 NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year by The Associated Press.<ref>{{cite news |author=The Associated Press |title=AP NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year Voting |url=https://apnews.com/article/nfl-defensive-rookie-award-voting-7d9224fa3a40677fb93dad0abac91bea |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 5, 2026 |access-date=May 29, 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Carter is [[Muslim]], and wore a [[thawb]] on draft day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Truax |first=Barkley |date=2025-04-24 |title=Look: Abdul Carter pays homage to religious roots with special NFL Draft outfit |url=https://www.on3.com/pro/news/abdul-carter-pays-homage-to-religious-roots-with-special-nfl-draft-outfit/ |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=On3 Pros |language=en}}</ref> He is nicknamed "Darth Vader" after the [[Darth Vader|character of the same name]] from the ''[[Star Wars]]'' franchise, notably donning the moniker on his [[eye black]] during games.<ref name="Vader">{{Cite web |last=Treacy |first=Dan |date=2025-01-10 |title=Abdul Carter eye black, explained: Why Penn State star has 'Darth Vader' on his face during Orange Bowl |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-football/news/abdul-carter-eye-black-penn-state-darth-vader-orange-bowl/60c98d6e32b93d6bb3092f6b |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=Sporting News}}</ref>

In April 2024, Carter was charged with a misdemeanor for assaulting a tow truck driver who was towing Carter's car for parking without a permit. Carter was accused of forcefully pulling the driver from his truck, throwing him to the ground and not allowing him to get up, leaving the driver with a fractured rib. '''Aaron Shampklin''' (born October 18, 1999) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Harvard Crimson football|Harvard Crimson]]. He played professionally for the [[Dallas Cowboys]], [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[Houston Roughnecks (2024)|Houston Gamblers]], [[Los Angeles Chargers]] and [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].

==Early life==
Shampklin was born in [[Paramount, California]], on October 18, 1999. He attended [[Long Beach Polytechnic High School]] in [[Long Beach, California|Long Beach]].

==College career==
Shampklin played [[college football]] at [[Harvard University]], where he graduated with a degree in economics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Shampklin - 2021 - Football |url=https://gocrimson.com/sports/football/roster/aaron-shampklin/23980 |access-date=2024-12-31 |website=Harvard University |language=en}}</ref>

In 2017, Shampklin scored his first career [[touchdown]] against [[Rhode Island Rams football|Rhode Island]]. He finished the year with 363 rushing yards and three TDs for the [[Harvard Crimson football|Crimson]]. In 2018, Shampklin played in all 10 games and was named first team All-[[Ivy League]]. He scored four touchdowns against [[San Diego Toreros football|San Diego]] along with a career-high 178 rushing yards. Shampklin finished with 1,053 rushing yards on 173 carries and nine touchdowns. Shampklin would not play the following two seasons, due to injury in 2019 and the 2020 cancellation and the [[Ivy League]] cancelling their 2020 football season. In 2021, Shampklin was name all-Ivy League for a second time. He ran for 835 yards and 11 touchdowns.
